## Phase 9: unit 9D1, OCCT.NET as build123d.NET's default backend

1299. **build123d.NET's default backend is OCCT.NET, from the packages** (unit 9D1; question 40, decision 1298).
       `Build123dBackend` defaults to `OcctNet`. `Build123d.OcctNet` references the four `OcctNet.*` packages from
       nuget.org at `OcctNetVersion` (0.1.0-preview.2, in build123d.NET's Directory.Build.props), so a fresh clone
       builds and tests with a plain `dotnet test`, with no OCCT.NET checkout and no native build. With `OcctNetRoot`
       given it references that checkout's projects, as before: for developing both together, and for
       `tools/pack-nuget.ps1`, which passes it. `OcctNetRoot` no longer defaults to `../OCCT.NET`: an implicit sibling
       would silently take the place of the packages.
1300. **Native is opt-in, the oracle's reference, and unpublished.** `-p:Build123dBackend=Native` builds and tests it
       as before. `Build123d.Occt`, and `Build123d` on the native backend, are packable only with `NativeStageDir`,
       which only build123d.NET's `tools/pack.ps1` passes; that script stays, for the native load-context test, packs
       into the local feed alone and versions the packages `0.1.0-native` so they can't be taken for the published
       ones. `Build123dNativeRoot` (default: the checkout itself) says whose `.deps/install` and `native/out` the
       native backend copies, so a worktree can use the main checkout's native build.
1301. **Output folders: the default in `bin`/`obj`, native in `bin-native`/`obj-native`.** The default gets the
       conventional folders; the two backends sit side by side. The old `bin-occtnet`/`obj-occtnet` stay excluded from
       the projects' items and ignored, for checkouts that still have them.
1302. **Tests on one backend.** `Build123d.Occt.Tests` is a test project on the native backend only (`IsTestProject`
       false otherwise, so `dotnet test` skips it with a message and still builds it). The packaging tests skip without
       their inputs (`B3D_PACKAGES`, set by `tools/pack.ps1`; `B3D_OCCTNET_LIB`). `Fillet2DTests.FilletRecord`, the one
       test that fails on OCCT.NET (a 2D fillet's history gives a wire's first vertex two modified shapes where native
       gives one, known since before phase 7), is a `KnownOcctNetDifferenceFact`: skipped on OCCT.NET with the reason,
       run natively. It is left for triage, not fixed here.
1303. **The oracle stays native: `AdditionalProperties` and graph restore.** The oracle tests and the benchmarks
       reference build123d.NET's `Build123d` and `Build123d.Occt` with `AdditionalProperties` =
       `$(Build123dNativeProperties)` (`Build123dBackend=Native;Build123dNativeRoot=...`, Directory.Build.props).
       NuGet's default restore walk ignores `AdditionalProperties` (it restores each project once, by path, with the
       entry's global properties), so it restored build123d.NET's projects on their default backend into `obj` and the
       native build then found no `obj-native/project.assets.json`. Restoring by the project graph
       (`RestoreUseStaticGraphEvaluation`, in Directory.Build.props for projects and in a new Directory.Solution.props
       for the solution) honours them. The oracle's and benchmarks' native check looks for b3docct under
       `Build123dNativeRoot` (default `Build123dNetRoot`). Against a build123d.NET checkout from before the switch the
       properties are harmless: `Native` was its default and it ignores `Build123dNativeRoot`.
## Phase 9: unit 9D2, the differential run

1304. **The differential run logs build123d.NET's shapes on both backends and compares the logs** (phase9-plan.md
       2.3). The plan's design was to record native's forwarded calls with their inputs and replay them on OCCT.NET. In
       its place, the suite runs once per backend, each logging its own results, and the logs are compared:
       - **Why:** a recording of every forwarded call would have to capture and rebuild every argument type the
         forwarding layer passes (adaptors, builders, lists, histories), in a generated hook in both bindings. A log of
         results needs one hook, in build123d.NET, and catches every operation the suite reaches, including
         build123d.NET's own code between kernel calls. What it gives up: a divergence late in a test is compared on
         the port's inputs, not native's; the report gives each test's *first* divergence, whose inputs are the same.
       - **The hook** (build123d.NET's `ShapeLog.cs`): with `BUILD123D_SHAPE_LOG` set, the `Shape` constructor and
         `Rewrapped` write each kernel shape whose TShape is new in the running test (not a sub-shape of one already
         logged) as BRep text, with the build123d call that made it and a digest of its vertices' exact points (BRep
         text has 15 digits). The running test is found on the stack. Off, it is one static field read; on, it only
         reads shapes. The suite runs one test at a time (`xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false`).
       - **The comparison** (`Build123dDifferentialTests`, an oracle test reading the logs from `B3D_DIFF_LOGS`;
         `tools/b3d-differential.ps1` runs everything): entry by entry, BRep text, then the Free flag masked, then the
         Free and Checked flags, then canonically (decision 581). Then two looser matches, each explained below: a
         located vertex's own coordinates, and results invalid on both sides. A test whose rest is canonically the same
         shapes in another order counts as the same. Native's other runs say where native varies from run to run.
1305. **Two kinds of entry are the same though their texts aren't** (unit 9D2).
       - **A located vertex's own coordinates.** BRepLib_MakeWire merges an edge's vertex onto the wire's in place
         (`BRep_Builder::UpdateVertex`), storing the point brought back through the vertex's location: `(p + t) - t`
         can differ from `p` by an ulp. Native rewrites the caller's vertex so; OCCT.NET leaves a frozen one as it is
         when the located point doesn't change (decisions 92 and 275). The located points are equal to the bit (the
         log's digest); 15-digit text can show the stored ones differ (build123d.NET's 2D fillets, `WireFillet.Splice`:
         9 entries). Mirroring the write (copying the frozen vertex whenever the round trip moves the stored point)
         matched native in a direct oracle case but not in the fillets' first splice, so it isn't kept.
       - **Invalid on both sides.** A fillet too large for its edges (`FilletFailuresTests.PlainMessage`, `MaxFillet`'s
         search) gives a shape BRepCheck rejects on both backends, and build123d.NET discards it with the same error.
         Phase 7's oracle compares failed fillets by their errors (decision 1164's tail); here 5 entries.
1306. **The differential run's result** (2 November 2026; OCCT.NET at phase 9's integration point with 9A,
       build123d.NET's `occtnet/p9d2`). Build123d.Tests: 1,858 tests natively (1,851 pass, 7 skipped), 1,881 on OCCT.NET
       (1,875 pass, 5 skipped, `Fillet2DTests.FilletRecord` fails as before), logged under 999 test methods.
       - **Logged:** 18,640 shapes natively, 18,661 on OCCT.NET. Compared up to each test's first divergence: 16,044.
         13,165 byte-identical; 1,290 with the Free flag masked; 663 with the Free and Checked flags masked; 160
         canonically identical (fillets and chamfers, offsets, sweeps of a frozen profile); 9 equal but for a located
         vertex's own coordinates and 5 invalid on both sides (decision 1305); 736 canonically identical in another
         order, in 18 tests (sub-shapes taken out of a canonically identical fillet, in its order); 16 first divergences
         of shapes (and 2 of counts, where a test logs fewer shapes on one side).
       - **Tests:** 938 the same throughout, 18 the same in another order, 25 logged by one backend only (tests under
         `#if OCCTNET` or native-only: STL, glTF, 3MF, STEP assemblies, the faults and memory pressure), 11 diverging
         where native varies from run to run (offsets in 2D and 3D, `Hollow`, wires joined or built from mixed edges,
         a random vertex; seen across 5 whole and 6 partial native runs), 7 attributed, **0 open**.
       - **Attributed** (in the test's table): STEP read through the assembly tree on OCCT.NET and shape-only natively
         (decision 1296), so the importer wraps other shapes on its way (3 tests); a theory row that returns early on
         OCCT.NET, misaligning its rows; `FilletRecord`, failing on OCCT.NET as recorded in build123d.NET's design.md;
         the introductory examples' `Extrude(both)`, whose two prisms share the sketch's face natively and hold copies
         of it on OCCT.NET (decisions 468, 1102), so their fuse differs; a test mutating the text of a fillet's result.
       - **Port bugs:** none found. Everything the suite makes is native's, byte for byte or canonically, or differs
         where native differs from itself or where OCCT.NET doesn't write a caller's shape.
## Phase 9: unit 9F, the triage of decision 1165's five cases

1307. **A sweep's copy for write is left as the sweep made it** (bugs/modalg_6/bug26406, a port bug; fixed). When the
       generating shape holds frozen TShapes, MakePrism, MakeRevol and MakePipe sweep an exact copy of it, then give
       back in the result the caller's sub-shapes the sweep left unchanged (`KeepUnchangedGenerating`). That step gave
       a changed copy (the paraboloid face's wire) its kept children in place, so the copy no longer held the sweep's
       own seam edge. BRepSweep reads its generating shape again for the history: `BRepSweep_Rotation::HasShape` finds
       a seam by walking the generating shape's faces, so `Generated(seam)` no longer saw a seam, built a face from it
       on demand and wrote a pcurve into the published result: `TopoDS_LockedShape` in Draw's `revol` (its history).
       Without copy, `IsDeleted(seam)` said true where native says false: bugs/modalg_7/bug30346_2 (decision 981) had
       the same cause and now passes. `BRepTools.KeepUnchangedIn` gains `theToLeaveCopies`: a changed copy holding kept
       children is replaced in the result by a new TShape (the copy's data and flags, the kept children), and the copy
       stays as it was; only MakeSweep asks for it (sewing and BRepFill go on reading the result's own TShapes).
       Second part: OCCT's history builds on demand the edge a vertex generates when no face built it (here the vertex
       on the paraboloid's seam and degenerated edge; native's `Generated` gives an edge that isn't in the result),
       and sets its vertices' parameters with `UpdateVertex(V, Par, E, PConfusion)`. On a FORWARD or REVERSED vertex
       that call changes only the edge's ranges and raises the vertex's tolerance to at least 1e-9, so natively it
       leaves the result's vertex as it is; the port threw on the frozen vertex. `BRep_Builder.UpdateVertexOfFrozen`
       (internal, `// OCCT.NET: frozen`) sets only the ranges then, as MakeWire's `transfert` does (decision 417's
       rule: writes that change nothing are skipped); any other write still throws. BRepSweep_Rotation and
       BRepSweep_Translation's `SetDirectingParameter` use it. Test: the oracle's
       `Sweeps_of_faces_with_a_seam_have_native_OCCTs_histories` (a cylinder, a sphere band and a sphere cap, frozen,
       revolved by π and 2π and extruded, with and without copy: 18 results equal to native's, 615 history values
       equal; it fails on both parts without the fix). bug26406's `revol` + `checkshape` pass.
1308. **The filling binds the boundary edges MakeWire copied** (bugs/filling/bug23380, a port bug; fixed).
       `BRepFill_Filling::BuildWires` joins the boundary edges with BRepLib_MakeWire; an edge meeting the wire only
       geometrically (b_3 at b_2's end) has its vertex merged onto the wire's, which MakeWire moves and enlarges in
       place natively. The caller's edges are frozen in the port, so MakeWire goes on with a copy for write of the
       wire built so far (decision 417); the filling then built its final edges from the caller's b_2 and f_1, whose
       vertices were not the copies the new b_3 ends at: WireFromList found no next edge and the face had 3 edges for
       4. `BuildWires` now binds, when MakeWire copied, each boundary edge to the edge standing for it in the finished
       wire (through MakeWire's `InternalHistory()`), as OCCT binds the geometrically joined ones, and records the
       copied vertices so that `Generated` of the caller's vertex answers as native's. bug23380's face is now byte for
       byte native's BRep text. The oracle's `MakeFilling_on_the_corpus_case_bug23380_matches_native_OCCT` read the
       case's words without the initial surface (filling's `a[5]`, here the face i) and so never met the merge; it now
       loads it as Draw does, and fails without the fix.
1309. **lowalgos/extss/bug29712_44 is OCCT's script**: it runs `extrema s1 s1` and `extrema s2 s2`, each plane against
       itself (distance 0), and expects 10, the distance between s1 and s2. Native OCCT gives 0 too
       (GeomAPI_ExtremaSurfaceSurface on the same planes: parallel, distance 0; 10 for s1 against s2). Attributed in
       DrawCheapGapsCorpusTests' known failures; occt-issues.md.
1310. **demo/samples/anc101 fails natively too.** The sample (resources/samples/tcl/ANC101.tcl) welds the platform
       and the wedge with `blend _model _model 2 _model_27`, then `_model_28`, numbered by one `explode _model e`;
       after the first blend the edge `_model_28` is no longer in the model, so the second blend has no suitable edge.
       Replayed natively from the port's primitives (a scratch recorder of the case's bcut, bfuse, unifysamedom and
       blend calls), native's own chain of Booleans gives the same model (the same counts at every step; the texts
       equal call by call in non-destructive mode, up to a few last-digit differences) and fails the same way on
       `_model_28`, destructive or not. The case then needs the viewer (`vbackground`, `vaspects`), outside the port
       anyway. Attributed in DrawFilletCorpusTests' known failures; occt-issues.md.
1311. **bugs/fclasses/bug1281 tests Draw's plugin loader**: `pload` reading a plugin resource file, loading the
       libraries it names and their Tcl scripts, going on past a missing one and failing when none loads. Draw-lite's
       commands are built in and its `pload` loads nothing (DrawBuiltins), so both checks fail. Out of scope;
       attributed in DrawCheapGapsCorpusTests' known failures.

## Phase 9: unit 9F2, build123d.NET's 2D fillet record

1312. **The 2D fillet's record differs because build123d.NET keeps MakeWire's intermediate edges; not a port bug.**
       build123d.NET's `Fillet2DTests.FilletRecord` (OCCT.NET backend) gave Modified(first vertex) = 2 where native
       gives 1. `WireFillet.Splice` adds the trimmed edges, the arc and the untouched edges to one
       BRepBuilderAPI_MakeWire and records, after each `Add`, the edge `Edge()` returns. Closing the wire, the last edge's
       vertex at the first corner (the same point, tolerance 1.0000000011e-7 from the splitter) merges onto the wire's
       first vertex (1e-7, the trimmed edge's), whose tolerance must grow. Native OCCT raises it in place, so the edge
       recorded first stays the wire's. That vertex is the caller's (frozen): the port's MakeWire goes on with a copy for
       write of the wire built so far (decision 417) and records the replacement in its history (`Modified`), so the
       first recorded edge and vertex are no longer the wire's, and the first vertex is recorded as modified into both
       copies. The port's MakeWire is right under the immutability rule; 9D2's abandoned change (`movesPoint`) concerned
       moved located vertices and would not prevent this copy (here the point is unchanged; the tolerance grows).
       Remedy, in build123d.NET (not made here): `Splice` adds all edges, builds, and records the finished wire's edges
       (its children in the order added) in place of each intermediate `Edge()`; the same on native, where they are the
       same shapes. Checked in a detached worktree of build123d.NET's main: Fillet tests 52/52 on OCCT.NET (FilletRecord
       passes) and 51/51 on native (scratchpad p9f2-b3d-wirefillet.diff).
## Phase 9: unit 9E, the performance review

1313. **Performance wins that keep native's results** (owner's answer, decision 1298: "only performance wins that keep
       native's results"; docs/performance.md). Profiles of build123d.NET's suite and of Bento's examples on OCCT.NET
       (EventPipe: CPU samples, allocations, exceptions, the JIT and the collector) found five cheap hot spots, each
       fixed without changing values, iteration order or tolerances:
       - `Intf_TangentZone` keeps its points in a deque: `PolygonInsert`'s insertions at the front were quadratic on a
         .NET list (OCCT's sequence is linked). `MaxFillet` went from 28 s to 2.8 s (native 0.8 s).
       - `NCollection_DynamicArray` takes its first capacity (the increment, at most 256) on the first element, as
         OCCT allocates its first block, not at construction; elements move at the same sizes as before, so a `ref`
         from `Append` stays valid as long as it did.
       - `BRepMesh_DataStructureOfDelaun`'s deleted links are a `Queue<int>` (OCCT's list is used only as a queue);
         `NCollection_CellFilter.Cell` copies its indexes with `ToArray`; `math_NewtonMinimum` subtracts in place.
       Serially, build123d.NET's suite went from 3.7× native's time to 1.9×; in parallel from 43–46 s to 18–21 s
       (native 3.4–3.9 s), where the garbage collector (17.5 GB allocated) and the JIT take most of what is left.
       Bento's examples recalculate in 1.5× native's time and open in 3.5× (the JIT).
1314. **Proposals left for the owner** (docs/performance.md, ranked): server GC or a larger gen-0 budget in hosts that
       compute in parallel (the suite 2× faster in parallel); ReadyToRun for the packages (opening 37% faster);
       `NCollection_List` as a linked list (5–10%, changes its public enumerator type); reusing
       `math_NewtonMinimum`'s work arrays; small math vectors on the stack; a deque for `NCollection_Sequence`; a cheaper
       identity hash for `TopoDS_TShape`, only if map iteration order is kept. Exceptions are not a cost (about 2,400
       in the whole suite). `benchmarks/OcctNet.Bento.Benchmarks` measures Bento's workload on either backend; it needs
       the build123d.NET checkout, so it is not in the solution.

## Phase 9: unit 9R, ReadyToRun packages

1315. **The packages are compiled ahead of time** (owner, 2 November, on unit 9E's proposals 1 and 2). `tools/pack-nuget.ps1`
       builds each of the six projects, publishes it with `PublishReadyToRun` for win-x64 (all six before any is
       swapped in, as publishing a project builds the ones it references again), puts each ReadyToRun assembly in place of
       its build output and packs without building again. The assemblies keep their IL: on another platform .NET ignores
       the precompiled code. The script checks the assemblies it packs and the ones the smoke test restores hold
       ReadyToRun code (the CLI header's ManagedNativeHeader). The packages grow about 2.5× (about 20 MB for the six);
       unit 9E measured the first opening of Bento's example workbook a third faster. `-NoReadyToRun` packs IL only.
       Proposal 1, the server garbage collector, is Bento's (its branch `perf/server-gc`).

1316. **Phase 9 closes with its three milestones met** (phase9-plan.md section 4; owner's answers, decision 1298).
       - **Published and consumed:** OcctNet.Foundation, ModelingData, ModelingAlgorithms, DataExchange,
         Build123d.OcctNet and Build123d on nuget.org as `0.1.0-preview.2` and `0.1.0-preview.3` (the owner pushed both),
         over Schematiq.Collections 1.0.0-beta.1 (unit 9A, decision 1297); `tools/pack-nuget.ps1` builds them in
         Release, ReadyToRun for win-x64 (unit 9R, decision 1315), and checks them from a clean feed. Bento's 3D models
         extension references them from nuget.org, the folder feed gone (unit 9C), and Bento uses the server garbage
         collector.
       - **The switch:** OCCT.NET is build123d.NET's default backend, from the packages (unit 9D1, decisions 1299 to
         1303); native OCCT is opt-in, the oracle's reference, unpublished. build123d.NET's whole suite compared on both
         backends shape by shape (unit 9D2, decisions 1304 to 1306): 16,044 shapes, 13,165 byte-identical, the rest
         equal under the oracle's masks, canonical or in another order, 0 open divergences. The five possible port bugs
         of decision 1165: two fixed (MakeSweep's history, the filling's edges; bug30346_2 passes too), three
         attributed (unit 9F, decisions 1307 to 1311); build123d.NET's FilletRecord fixed in build123d.NET (1312).
       - **Measured:** docs/performance.md (unit 9E, decisions 1313, 1314). build123d.NET's suite on OCCT.NET from 3.7×
         native's time to 1.9× serially; Bento's examples recalculate at 1.5×; the server collector and ReadyToRun
         taken from the proposals, the rest left for phase 10.
       - **Port status** unchanged at 62.0%: phase 9 ported nothing new.

## Phase 10: preparation

1317. **Phase 10: Kerf** (owner, 2 November; phase10-plan.md). The owner's brief: .NET conventions over OCCT's and
       build123d's; full immutability with no copy at entry, sharing unchanged faces; OCCT's bugs may be fixed; the
       oracle may go once testing shows every feature works; results rather than expected exceptions; .NET 10 and C#'s
       latest features; value types, spans and fitting collections; build123d.NET on OCCT.NET's types directly, without
       Python conventions, its native backend retired. Then:
       - **One repository** for OCCT.NET and build123d.NET (unit 10R), the layers kept as separate assemblies and
         packages under their own licences (LGPL 2.1 with OCCT's exception; Apache 2.0).
       - **The name is Kerf**, in Renegade Dynamics' organisation: `Kerf.Kernel` (from OCCT 8.0.1) and `Kerf.Modeling`
         (from build123d), each crediting its origin as its licence requires; OCCT's names and marks kept out of the
         product's name.
       - Questions 46 to 52: the namespaces `Kerf.<Area>`, `Kerf.Engine.<Area>` and `Kerf.Modeling`; Bento's
         spreadsheet-facing names renamed to follow Kerf's; the coverage floor (every public member, 80% per engine
         package); standard .NET read-only collections in both layers, Bento converting to Schematiq.Collections only
         when it modifies one and Schematiq.Collections implementing the .NET read-only interfaces; Draw-lite kept;
         phase 9 closed at `0.1.0-preview.3`.

## Phase 10: unit 10R, one repository

1318. **OCCT.NET and build123d.NET in one repository, Kerf** (github.com/renegadedynamics/kerf; decision 1317). Each
       project's `main` history moved into its own folder with `git filter-repo --to-subdirectory-filter` (OCCT.NET to
       `kernel/`, build123d.NET to `modeling/`) and merged with `--allow-unrelated-histories`, so `git log` and `blame`
       reach back through both. Each folder keeps its licence, notices, docs, CHANGELOG and solution; the root README
       explains the two layers and credits OCCT and build123d.
       - **Wiring:** the modeling layer builds against `../kernel/`'s projects by default (`OcctNetRoot`), or the
         nuget.org packages with `-p:UseOcctNetPackages=true`; the kernel finds build123d.NET in `../modeling/`
         (`Build123dNetRoot`), its native build where `Build123dNativeRoot` says.
       - **Kerf.slnx** holds everything but what runs native OCCT: the kernel's oracle tests and native benchmarks, the
         modeling layer's native backend, its tests and generator. One restore can't serve the modeling projects on both
         backends at once: graph restore loses the kernel's references from build123d.NET's tests, and the default
         restore ignores the oracle's `AdditionalProperties`, so the native copies see both backends' types. The oracle
         tests run on their own (`tools/merge/merge-unit.sh` runs them after Kerf.slnx, against
         `BUILD123D_NATIVE_ROOT`). Units 10A and 10B retire native, and with it the split.
       - **No behaviour changed:** the same tests pass as in the two repositories.
       - The merge tooling's paths are the repository's (`kernel/docs/decisions.md`, `kernel/CHANGELOG.md`,
         `modeling/CHANGELOG.md`); the old repositories stay as they are until archived.

## Phase 10: unit 10C, conventions and tooling

1319. **The renamer is a single-pass Roslyn tool, not Roslyn's `Renamer`** (tools/kerf-rename; phase10-plan.md 2.3).
       It loads the solution once with MSBuildWorkspace, plans every rename from the map and the rules, scans every
       document in parallel binding only tokens whose text is a planned old name, and rewrites the text. Measured on
       Kerf.slnx: 45 s for all of OcctNet.Foundation (20,100 renames, 258,000 edits) and 47 s for
       ModelingAlgorithms (84,000 renames, 456,000 edits), dry runs of drafted maps; about four minutes for the
       whole kernel. `Renamer.RenameSymbolAsync` takes 0.1 to 3 s a symbol once warm, but each call forks the
       solution, and it can't convert methods to properties, move namespaces or apply the collision rules. The scope is one assembly, optionally narrowed to OCCT packages; references are
       updated in every project of the solution given, so the same tool and map update Bento's repository later.
1320. **The name map is a sorted line-based text file** (`kind id new-name  # note`), keyed by Roslyn's documentation
       comment ids, which are the same for source and metadata. Kinds: `rule`, `package`, `type`, `member`,
       `property` (a method becoming a get-only property), `param`, `alias`, `keep`. `kerf-rename draft` writes the
       systematic part for review; `apply --applied` writes the map as applied, with a `keep` line and its reason for
       every rename the run dropped: that map, not the reviewed one, is what other repositories apply and what is
       kept for finding OCCT's names (2.3).
1321. **The systematic rules** (design-rules.md section 1): parameters `theX` and OCCT's older PascalCase ones to
       camelCase; non-public instance fields (protected included) `myX`/`x` to `_x`; non-public static fields to
       `s_x`, or PascalCase when constant or read-only; locals `aX`/`anX` and PascalCase ones to camelCase; camelCase
       methods to PascalCase; `NbXxx()` to an `XxxCount` property and `IsXxx()`/`HasXxx()` to properties, drafted only
       where the method is a cheap getter (an expression, or a return behind at most two guards). **Collisions are
       dropped and reported, never guessed:** a name another symbol in the same body or type hierarchy already has,
       a reserved word, a method used as a delegate or implementing an interface. Where a new name would mean
       something else at a reference (a member `Scale` hiding `TransformForm.Scale`), the reference is qualified in
       full rather than the rename dropped.
1322. **The pilot's names are drafts for 10D**, kept in kernel/docs/phase10/pilot-gp-math.map on the unmerged pilot
       branch: `Kerf.Geometry` with a `2D`/`3D` suffix where a type has a 2D twin (`Point3D`, `Point2D`, `Frame3D`,
       `Transform3D`), none otherwise (`Plane`, `Sphere`); OCCT's `math` in `Kerf.Engine.Numerics`, never a namespace
       `…Math`, which would capture every `Math.Sqrt` beneath it.
1323. **The pilot (branch `phase10/u10c-pilot`, not merged)**: gp and math renamed across Kerf.slnx, 94 types, 67 methods made
       properties, 5,500 renames in all, 102,513 edits in 2,421 files, in 33 s.
       Kerf.slnx builds with no error and no change by hand; the Foundation (2,206), ModelingData (3,125),
       ModelingAlgorithms (4,709 and 9 skipped) and modelling-layer (1,876 and 5 skipped) tests pass. DataExchange passes 265 of 266: `StepGenTests.CommittedSourcesAreTheGeneratorsOutput`
       fails because stepgen still writes OCCT's names into the STEP classes it generates, so in 10E the generators
       (stepgen, and the forwarding layer's until 10B removes it) must take the map too.
       What it showed the tool must handle, and now does: indexer accessors' parameters, `global::` inside an
       interpolation hole (read as a format), calls made as statements (`x.NbSolutions();` → `_ = x.SolutionCount;`),
       committed generated files, alias declarations, a converted method implementing an interface in a derived test
       class. What it can't, and reports: strings naming types (335 in gp and math, mostly `ToString()`'s
       `"gp_Pnt(…)"` and exception messages), `UnsafeAccessorType` strings, generators still writing OCCT's names,
       types sharing a file with types going elsewhere (2). Not reached by Kerf.slnx: the oracle tests and benchmarks
       (kernel/OcctNet.slnx), which need a run of their own.
1324. **Naming is stated in a root .editorconfig and turned on package by package in 10E** (design-rules.md section
       14): 10E first removes IDE1006 from kernel/Directory.Build.props' `NoWarn`, sets `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` and
       lists every unrenamed folder with IDE1006 off; each rename commit removes its folders from the list. Nothing
       changes in this unit's build. IDE1006 needs an explicit `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE1006.severity` to be reported by
       the build. Measured on the pilot: 30 of gp and math's 1,576 naming warnings remain, each needing a map entry.
1325. **The analyzers:** OCCTNET0001 (mutating calls on read-only struct values) is kept: `[InlineArray]` buffers and
       span views stay mutable structs. OCCTNET0002 (maps of shapes without a comparer) is kept but must be rewritten
       before TopoDS or NCollection is renamed: it finds its types by name (`Occt.NCollection_Map`1`, `TopoDS_Shape`,
       the namespace `Occt`), so a rename silently disables it. Immutability analyzers KERF0101 to KERF0107 are
       proposed for 10G and 10L (design-rules.md section 14), not written.
1326. **design-rules.md replaces translation-rules.md for new and redesigned code**; translation-rules.md stays as the
       rules the port followed until phase 10, marked so.

## Phase 10: unit 10K, OCCT's bugs triaged

1327. **The triage of occt-issues.md's 1,154 rows** (phase10-plan.md 2.8; docs/occt-issues-triage.md). Each row gets
       one class, in a new last column of every table:
       - **fix**, when a user can see the bug through a public operation: wrong geometry, topology or a property;
         a spurious failure (an exception or "not done") on valid input; a hang, or minutes where seconds are due; a
         file written invalid, or data lost reading or writing one. The effect must be shown at a public operation
         (the row's example, a recording, build123d.NET's use) or the class must be public API that callers use
         directly (gp, the 2D constraint solvers, the properties, GeomAPI).
       - **touch** (fix when touched), when the bug is real but its effect stays inside an algorithm or needs misuse
         to reach: arrays not indexed from 1, a working object reused, invalid input (10F's errors), statics (10I),
         copy at entry and in-place writes (10H), NCollection (10J), reports (10F). Intersection and Boolean internals
         (IntPolyh, IntPatch, IntWalk, IntTools, BOPDS, the pave filler) are touch even where a result moves: a fix
         there shifts Boolean results across the corpus with no shown benefit. A touch row becomes fix when a case
         shows a user the effect.
       - **leave**: cosmetic, documentation, dead or latent code, declared and never defined, uninitialised natively
         but deterministic in the port, native non-determinism the port lacks, test scripts and Draw's own command
         bugs (Draw-lite keeps OCCT's commands as the corpus harness, question 51).
       - **settled**: the port already doesn't reproduce the bug (a hang fixed minimally, untrusted-input guards,
         copies instead of in-place writes, port bugs fixed); the row stays as history.
       The result: 134 fix (133 distinct; units 8D and 8E repeat 13 rows of 8C1 and 8A2), 572 touch, 313 leave, 135
       settled. open-questions.md item 10's four examples are all fix.
1328. **The fix rows go in eight batches, in order of user impact**, each a unit's worth: K1 Booleans, bounding
       boxes and distances; K2 hangs and spurious failures; K3 wrong geometry from construction; K4 the 2D constraint
       solvers build123d.NET's constrained lines and arcs use; K5 properties and approximation errors; K6 extrema and
       projection; K7 curve and surface evaluation and conversion, gp; K8 data exchange. **A fix is recorded** in one
       commit with its test, never mixed with renames: the `// OCCT` marker goes; the test that pinned OCCT's value
       asserts the corrected behaviour against an independent reference, never a native value; each 10A recording it
       moves drops to "geometrically equal" or "intended difference" citing the row and the decision; the row's
       Triage cell becomes `fixed (decision N)`, the rest of the row unchanged; a build123d.NET workaround of the bug
       goes in the same unit. The markers can't be matched to rows mechanically (porting notes also start
       `// OCCT`): by class, 778 rows have a bug note in their class's files, 201 have none, and 126 bug-like markers
       in 95 files belong to classes with no row; both lists are in the triage's appendices.
## Phase 10: unit 10D, the public API design

1329. **The public/engine split is data, generated by rule** (docs/api/classification-rules.txt, read by
       tools/api-classify.cs into docs/api/classification.tsv): a rule per OCCT package and exceptions per type,
       checked so that every public type has a rule, no two types share a name, and no public type takes a common .NET
       type's name. Of the 3,892 public types (nested included; the plan's 4,027 counted source declarations), 102
       become public API as they are (gp's values, Geom's and Geom2d's curves and surfaces, TopoDS's shapes, four
       enums), 3,749 engine and 41 removed. With about 75 new types (operations, options, results, evaluators, mesh and
       exchange types), the public surface is about 170 types. Pending the owner's review (questions 53 to 65).
1330. **Engine types become internal per area at the end of 10L, not in 10E.** Public types expose engine types in
       their signatures today (`gp_Pnt.Coord()` returns `gp_XYZ`; Geom derives from `Standard_Transient`), which C#
       rejects once the engine is internal, so 10E renames and moves only. 479 engine types are used across the
       kernel's assemblies, so the proposal keeps `InternalsVisibleTo` among the four and to Draw-lite and the tests
       (question 54). Draw-lite stays on the engine permanently.
1331. **Engine namespaces by area with sub-namespaces**, `Kerf.Engine.<Area>[.<Sub>]` (`Kerf.Engine.Exchange.Step.Geometry`),
       chosen so no two types collide; where two packages share one, a prefix or suffix keeps them apart (`2D` for
       Geom2d's twins, `Fixer` for ShapeFix, `Check` for BRepCheck, `Step` for StepGeom's and StepShape's entities).
       Removed types keep their OCCT names in `Occt` until 10J (question 58).
1332. **One result type with history for shapes:** `Result<T>` (a struct: value or failure, with `Diagnostics`, each
       a severity, a string-backed code, a plain message and the shapes concerned) and `Built<TShape>` (the shape and
       its `ShapeHistory`, converting implicitly to the shape). Cancellation throws `OperationCanceledException`;
       misuse throws .NET's argument exceptions. Compiled in a scratch project with C# 14, not committed: 10F adds
       them with tests.
1333. **Operations are extension members in one static class per area** (`BooleanOperations`, `FilletOperations`…),
       callable as `BooleanOperations.Fuse(a, b)` and `a.Fuse(b)`, with factories as static extension members
       (`Solid.Box`); the signature order is inputs, an options record, `IProgress<double>?`, `CancellationToken`
       (question 53).
1334. **gp's structs are the public values directly**, renamed with a `3D`/`2D` suffix on every value that is a shape
       of space (`Point3D`, `Plane3D`, `Cylinder3D`), so none collides with System.Numerics or Kerf.Modeling; `gp_XYZ`,
       `gp_Quaternion` and the interpolators stay engine. **`TopoDS_Shape` is the public `Shape`**, with the typed
       sub-shapes as structs converting to it, a generic `IShape<T>` for traversal, and `ShapeComparer.Same`/`Equal`.
1335. **The draft name map** (docs/api/kerf.map) is kerf-rename's draft over the four assemblies seeded by the
       classification, then finished by `api-classify.cs --finish-map`: removed types' entries dropped, OCCT's
       capitalised enum members in PascalCase. 3,693 types, 1,817 members, 1,616 methods made properties.
## Phase 10: unit 10A, test independence

1336. **The oracle tests call native OCCT through a recorded facade** (phase10-plan.md 3.1). The 383 tests stay where
       they are (`tests/OcctNet.Oracle.Tests`), converted in place rather than rewritten one by one: `N` now names
       `OcctNative`, a facade with the 2,230 members of build123d.NET's native wrappers the tests use (299 types),
       generated by `tools/oracle-facade.cs` from the test assembly's references (`Recorded/Native.g.cs`). Each member
       is a step on the running test's tape (`Recorded/NativeTape.cs`):
       - **Replaying** (the default): the step's results are read from the test's recording, embedded in the assembly
         (`Recordings/<class>.tape.gz`, one tape per test method or theory row): values, the types of the objects
         returned, the exception thrown, the files native OCCT wrote (`BRepTools::Write`, STEP files). The step is
         checked first: the member, and a byte of a running hash of every call's arguments (numbers to the bit, facade
         objects by their number on the tape, rooted paths by their file's content, a STEP file's time stamp left
         out). The port's side always runs, so each test compares the port with native's results exactly as it did
         live: its masks, canonical forms and tolerances unchanged.
       - **Recording** (`OCCTNET_ORACLE_RECORD=1`, built with native OCCT): each step runs natively
         (`Recorded/Native.Record.g.cs`, compiled only with `HAS_ORACLE`, which 10B deletes) and is written to the tape.
       - **Live** (`-p:OracleDirect=true`): the tests compile against `Build123d.Occt` itself, as before; the facade's
         generator reads that build.
       - **Why a tape and not a rewrite:** 61,000 lines of tests, each comparing in its own way, keep their comparisons
         exactly; what native told them becomes data. A port change that alters what a test asks native OCCT fails at
         that step, saying so, rather than comparing with an answer to another question.
       - **build123d.NET's scenarios** (`Build123d/`) run build123d.NET on native OCCT, so only when recording. What
         they produce is recorded as values (`Tape.Value`): the Boolean and phase 7 captures (their calls, with native
         shapes adopted into the facade), build123d.NET's fillet messages; `Build123dConstructionOracleTests` now
         records cases (kind, operands as native OCCT writes them, data as JSON) and runs them
         (`Build123dConstructionScenarios.cs` holds the scenarios). Static native objects were made per test.
1337. **Budgets keep the recordings small.** Everything native returned came to 2.3 GB compressed (mostly corpora
       written as BRep text and meshes read triangle by triangle). The loops that made it run under `Tape.Budget`: when
       recording, a loop takes items while its recording stays under 750 kB (uncompressed), a corpus's in a spread
       order (every seventh first) and without its largest files; the replay takes the items recorded. The random
       tests' counts are `Tape.Cases(live, recorded)`, scaled to the same budget. Coverage floors that counted the
       whole corpus (`> 2000 files`) hold live only. Live (`OracleDirect`) everything runs in full. The recordings:
       117 files, 109 MB, the largest 4.6 MB (GeomAPI_IntSS); a re-recording replaces them whole, so history grows by
       about that much each time.
1338. **The differential run's native log is recorded, reduced** (decisions 1304 to 1306). Native's full log (18,640
       shapes as BRep text) is too large to commit sensibly. `Recordings/Build123dDifferential.native.gz` keeps, per
       test and entry, the header, the digests of the BRep text as is, with the Free flag masked and with the Free and
       Checked flags masked, the properties (sub-shape counts, volume, area, bounding box), and the full text only from
       a test's first entry that OCCT.NET's log didn't match under the masks when recorded; and where native's two runs
       first differ. `tools/b3d-differential.ps1` now runs build123d.NET's suite on OCCT.NET only, then the comparison
       against the recording; `-Record -NativeRoot` records native's log again (two native runs) while native OCCT
       exists. An entry byte-identical when recorded that later differs is reported with both sides' properties.
       Recorded from six native runs (2.5 MB): 999 tests, 18,640 native shapes; against OCCT.NET's log, 16,148 compared
       before any divergence (13,270 byte-identical), 941 tests the same throughout, 9 where native varies, 6
       attributed, 0 open, as 9D2 found (decision 1306). Two native runs left three tests' native variance unseen (the
       joined wires and 2D offsets of decision 1306), so six are recorded.
1339. **The oracle tests join Kerf.slnx** (decision 1318's split): without native OCCT they replay, so the merge gate
       runs them with everything else; recording builds them on their own with native OCCT.
1340. **Coverage** (plan 3.2, question 49): `tools/coverage.ps1` runs the kernel's unit tests, the Draw-lite tests (their
       default samples) and the modeling suite under Microsoft's code coverage (Cobertura, part of
       Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk), and `tools/coverage-report.cs` merges the runs into `docs/coverage.md`: line coverage per
       OCCT package (the folder under each kernel assembly) and per folder of the modeling layer, the packages under
       80% listed. Measured on 3 November: 77.4% of 581,793 coverable lines. The kernel: Foundation 77.4%,
       ModelingData 89.2%, ModelingAlgorithms 82.6%, DataExchange 58.0% (STEP's entity classes and their readers and
       writers, many reached by no test); 95 of its 245 packages are under 80% (41 in DataExchange, 28 in
       ModelingAlgorithms, 13 each in Foundation and ModelingData), listed for the later units, not filled here. The
       modeling layer's Build123d: 88.8%. Under instrumentation the runs take about two hours (ModelingAlgorithms.Tests
       53 minutes, the Draw-lite tests about an hour); `-Only` runs some.
1341. **What goes with native in 10B:** the 5 `NativeFact` tests (`FaultTests` 3, `MemoryPressureTests` 2, skipped on
       OCCT.NET), `Build123d.Occt.Tests` (12 tests of the shim), `Build123d.Packaging.Tests`' load-context test, the
       native benchmarks, `Recorded/Native.Record.g.cs`, `tools/oracle-facade.cs` and the record and live modes. Checked
       to need nothing native: the 30 STEP references (`Reference/Exchange`: `StepNativeTests` and `StepAssemblyTests`,
       30 tests) and Python build123d's `geometry.json`/`topology.json` (`ReferenceTests`, `TopologyReferenceTests`),
       116 tests passing on OCCT.NET with no Python and no native build.

## Phase 10: unit 10B, build123d.NET on OCCT.NET alone

1342. **OCCT.NET's exceptions reach build123d.NET's callers as they are** (the brief: "OCCT.NET's exceptions stay as
       they are until 10F"). A failure in the kernel is OCCT.NET's `Standard_Failure` subclass (`Standard_DomainError`,
       `StdFail_NotDone`…, with `OcctType`) with OCCT's message; where build123d.NET threw `OcctException` itself it
       throws the OCCT.NET type it named (`Standard_ConstructionError`, `Storage_StreamFormatError`). `OcctException`
       and `OcctContext` went with the forwarding layer that made them: the message no longer starts with what was
       being done ("box 0.0 × 1.0 × 1.0 failed: …"), which Bento shows in a cell until 10F's diagnostics replace it.
       Catch sites catch `Standard_Failure`; the tests assert OCCT.NET's types (`ThrowsAny<Standard_Failure>`), and
       the three tests of `OcctContext`'s scopes went.
1343. **The oracle replays only; the recordings are frozen** (decision 1341). Gone: recording
       (`OCCTNET_ORACLE_RECORD`, `HAS_ORACLE`, `Recorded/Native.Record.g.cs`, `RecordedNative`), the live mode
       (`OracleDirect`), `tools/oracle-facade.cs` (the facade `Recorded/Native.g.cs` is committed code now, frozen),
       build123d.NET's scenarios that ran on native OCCT (`Build123dConstructionScenarios.cs` and the captures'
       scenario code: their results are recorded values, read with `Tape.Value(what, read)`), `Build123dNativeRoot`,
       `Build123dNativeProperties`, the static-graph restore settings (and both `Directory.Solution.props`) native's
       project references needed, `b3d-differential.ps1 -Record -NativeRoot` and `B3D_DIFF_RECORD`. The tape's
       recording code went (`TapeWriter`, `Recorders`); the sampled limits stay (`Tape.Cases` is the recorded count,
       the corpus floors their recorded values). 383 tests pass, as recorded. The benchmarks lose their native
       comparisons (`HAS_NATIVE`, the phase 7 suite, the Bento benchmark's native project); their tables' native
       columns repeat the port's, as without native before. They build again: since 10A they needed native OCCT to
       compile.
1344. **build123d.NET calls OCCT.NET's types directly; `Build123d.OcctNet` is gone** (plan 2.9). Its 257 generated
       wrappers and 3,310 hand-written lines went; nothing of it is left. What the runtime did:
       - `Quantity_Color` (its 1,670-line port): OCCT.NET's own, ported since.
       - `Extras.ExtractMesh`, `MeshBuffers`: OCCT.NET's `MeshExtraction`, called directly.
       - `Extras.CopyHistory`: `BRepTools_History`'s public copy constructor (decision 1104).
       - `TopoDS_Builder`, the open-until-read shape, `BRep_Builder`: the kernel's builders (decision 1346), mostly
         their frozen forms (`TopoDS_Builder.MakeCompound`, `MakeShell`, `MakeSolid`).
       - `BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`, `BRepLib.BuildCurves3d`, the shape's in-place forms: their callers take the
         meshed shape from `Shape()`, `BRepLib.Curves3dBuilt`'s result, `Located`/`Reversed`.
       - `Collections.cs`: OCCT.NET's NCollection types, maps of shapes with `TopTools_ShapeMapHasher`.
       - `Extras` (BRep bytes with the native reader's checks, the memory estimate, alerts, an edge's own curve) and
         `Exchange.cs` (STEP through STEPCAFControl, the mesh formats, `ExchangeNode` and the limits): build123d.NET's
         glue, internal in `src/Build123d/Kernel`, until 10L gives them a public form in the kernel (questions 59, 60
         and 62). The STEPControl stream forms went, with the native fallback that used them.
       - `OcctObject`, `Occt.Version`, `FaultForTesting`, memory pressure (`AddMemoryPressure`, `Shape.Result` now the
         identity), `StepKeepsAssemblies` (always true): gone with native.
       OCCT.NET's values are structs, so `Build123d` asks a shape its kind (`IsCompound()`, `TopoDS.Compound(shape)`,
       `Kernel/ShapeExtensions.cs`) where it matched the wrappers' subclasses, takes outputs as `out`/`ref`, changes
       values through their twins (`WithRotation`, `Added`), uses nullable structs for absent shapes, and disposes
       nothing. No behaviour changed but decision 1345's: the 1,876 tests that passed pass.
1345. **A wire's `Triangulate` and `TriangulateTree` work** (found by the differential run). They threw
       `InvalidCastException` on both backends: the binding returned the meshed copy as a plain `TopoDS_Shape` wrapper,
       which `Wire.Edges` couldn't cast to `TopoDS_Wire`. On OCCT.NET's structs the cast is a check of the kind, and
       passes. Kept, with a test (`ShapeMeshTests.AWireTriangulates`); the differential run attributes the copy's edges
       native never logged (`InputsUnchangedTests.NoParameterlessMemberChangesItsShape`). The run: 999 tests, 939 the same
       throughout, 18 in another order, 9 where native varies, 7 attributed, 26 logged by one side only (renamed or
       removed tests among them), 0 open.
1346. **The members the `UnsafeAccessor`s reached are public**, as engine API until 10L makes the engine internal:
       `TopoDS_Builder`'s constructor, `MakeWire`, `MakeShell`, `MakeSolid`, `MakeCompSolid`, `MakeCompound` (by
       `ref`), `Add` and `Remove`; `BRep_Builder` (the class) and its `MakeFace(ref face, triangulation)`;
       `TopoDS_TShape.FreezeGraph`. That is 11 of the 14 accessors; the other three read `BRepTools_History`'s maps to
       copy it, which its public copy constructor does, so its fields stay private. `PublicBuilderTests` checks the
       members are public, and that a shape they build stays open until frozen.
1347. **`UseOcctNetPackages` is gone**, with `OcctNetVersion`: `Build123d` uses decision 1346's members, which
       0.1.0-preview.3 doesn't make public, so it builds against the kernel's projects only (`OcctNetRoot`), which
       pack as the package dependencies. `kernel/tools/pack-nuget.ps1` packs the five assemblies from the repository's
       HEAD (no second checkout), into `nuget-release` beside the repository; `Build123d.Packaging.Tests` loads
       `Build123d` and the kernel's four assemblies. Gone with native: `modeling/tools/pack.ps1` and the native
       packages' load-context test.
1348. **The native backend is gone** (decision 1341): `Build123d.Occt` (its 269 generated and hand-written files),
       `Build123d.Occt.Tests`, `tools/OcctGen`, `tools/OcctNetGen`, `generate-bindings.ps1`, `generate-occtnet.ps1`,
       `bindings`, `native` (the superbuild and the shim), the `Build123dBackend` switch, `bin-native`/`obj-native`,
       the `OCCTNET` define (its code kept), the five `NativeFact` tests. About 137,000 lines for native and 70,000 for
       the forwarding layer. build123d.NET's suite: 1,872 tests (1,881, less the five `NativeFact`s, the forwarding
       layer's `WhatIsntPortedSaysSo`, three `OcctContext` scope tests and a memory-pressure test, plus decision
       1345's), all passing. The tests keep their names where native's differential log is recorded under them.

## Phase 10: the owner's answers to questions 53 to 65 (10D's API design)

1349. **The owner's answers to questions 53 to 65**, agreed on 3 November 2026. They settle 10D's draft (kernel/docs/api) for 10E and 10L:

- **53, operations:** each area's operations are static methods on an `<Area>Operations` class and also C# 14 extension
  members, so `BooleanOperations.Fuse(a, b)` and `a.Fuse(b)` both work. design-rules.md's `Booleans.Fuse` example
  follows.
- **54, assemblies:** the four kernel assemblies stay, with `InternalsVisibleTo` between them, and to Kerf.Modeling until
  10M moves it onto the public API.
- **55, the transient base:** `Standard_Transient` stays public (as `Kerf.Engine.Foundation.Transient` in 10D's map), with
  no public members; 10J revisits it.
- **56, shape names:** the modelling layer uses the kernel's shapes directly (`Shape`, `Edge`, `Face` and so on), and keeps
  its own names only for modelling ideas (`Part`, `Sketch`, `Curve`). One set of shapes, not two.
- **57, dimension suffixes:** `2D`/`3D` where both versions exist (`Point3D`, `Vector2D`, `Plane3D`), none where only one
  does (`Surface`).
- **58:** types 10J will replace keep their OCCT names until then.
- **59, meshing:** returns a separate mesh value (`ShapeMesh`); faces don't hold triangles.
- **60, colour:** a root-level `Kerf.Color`, its public values in sRGB, as people write colours; it converts to linear
  where a format needs it (glTF). This replaces 10D's `Kerf.Exchange.ColorRgba` stored as linear.
- **61, diagnostics:** codes are strings, like analyzer IDs.
- **62, placement:** the public `Placement` compares by value, as .NET users expect. The engine keeps comparing locations
  by identity internally, where deciding whether two shapes are the same depends on it.
- **63:** STEP's entity classes become internal, and their 1,556 setters leave 10G's scope.
- **64, images:** the owner wants Kerf and Bento to generate both **SVG line drawings** and **PNG shaded pictures**.
  - **SVG:** a public hidden-line API (projection, visible and hidden edges, from HLRBRep) and an SVG writer, in 10L.
  - **PNG:** a managed software renderer drawing `ShapeMesh` values (a z-buffered rasteriser with simple shading and
    optional edges), with a PNG encoder, in 10L.
  - **Bento:** spreadsheet functions to make both, in 10N.
  - Hidden-line removal isn't needed for shaded pictures: Bento's model view draws meshes. 10D's "no public HLR API" is
    reversed.
- **65, namespaces:** `Kerf.Fillets`, `Kerf.Offsets`, `Kerf.Features`, `Kerf.Healing` and `Kerf.Measurement` are added.

## Phase 10: unit 10E, the rename

1350. **The map applied is 10D's draft, settled by decision 1349** (docs/api/kerf.map). `2D`/`3D` only where both
       versions exist (57): gp's `Cone`, `Cylinder`, `Sphere`, `Torus` and `CoordinateSystem` lose the suffix the draft
       gave them; `Plane3D` keeps it, `Plane` being System.Numerics's (design-rules 1). Removed types (NCollection,
       TCollection, `PackedList`, `TopoDS_HShape`) keep their OCCT names in `Occt` (58). `Standard_Transient` is
       `Kerf.Engine.Foundation.Transient` (55), `TopLoc_Location` is `Kerf.Topology.Placement` (62; its value equality
       is 10L's), the namespaces are 65's, and the shapes are `Kerf.Topology.Shape`, `Vertex` … `Compound` (56).
       Settled in 10E, each marked `10E` in the map: the 779 internal types the draft lacked (by the same scheme: STEP's
       readers and writers in `….ReadWrite`, `RWPlane`); interfaces prefixed `I`; exceptions ending in `Exception`,
       avoiding .NET's own names (`ZeroDivisorException`, `NumericOverflowException`); and, because each would bind a
       reference to the wrong symbol or not compile: no type named as a namespace or after its own namespace, as a type
       of the namespaces the code imports (`Stream`, `ConsoleColor`, `Parallel`, `Vector3`), as its base type, as a
       member of its own, as a type of an enclosing namespace (`BRep_TEdge` is `BrepTEdge`, `CPnts_AbscissaPoint`
       `CurveAbscissaPoint`), or starting with a digit (`TopOpeBRepTool_2d` is `Legacy2D`); and every engine type of
       ModelingAlgorithms and DataExchange named uniquely (177 renamed, prefixed by their namespace's last word:
       `BRepLib_MakeEdge` is `LibraryMakeEdge`), as a file importing two namespaces can't name a shared one.
1351. **A method renamed into another method's name takes `Core`** (`length` is `LengthCore`, `send` `SendCore`).
       kerf-rename now reports every rename that would merge two differently named methods into one set of overloads,
       not only those that would collide: `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint.length(…, double?)` beside `Length(…, double)` made the
       public overload call itself (the tests' stack overflow). Foundation's seven such methods, renamed before the rule,
       were checked by hand: their overloads can't be confused.
1352. **OCCT's names stay where OCCT prints, looks up or recorded them.** `OcctTypeNames` (Foundation, generated by
       `tools/occt-type-names.py` from the map) gives each renamed type's and enum member's OCCT name.
       `Transient.DynamicTypeName()` and `FailureException.OcctType` use it, and so does every place that used a type's
       .NET name as OCCT's `DynamicType()->Name()`: message keys (`Message_Algorithm` looks its texts up by class name),
       STEP's type signatures and statistics, the geometry hashers (which hash the type's name), exception names in
       messages. The kernel's tests, the oracle's and the differential log compare type, exception and enum names with
       native OCCT's recordings, so they print OCCT's names too; the oracle's tape finds a theory row recorded under an
       enum's OCCT name. Elsewhere enum values print with their new names (`Face`, not `Extrema_Face`).
1353. **Parameters and locals that would collide keep their names** (`thePoint` beside a local `point`): kerf-rename
       drops them, and IDE1006 is off in the 158 folders that still hold them or other leftovers (15306).
1354. **Enum members are named with their enum.** Before ModelingAlgorithms' rename, every member of its and
       DataExchange's enums that code named bare through `using static` was written qualified (OCCT's prefixed names are
       unique, so the qualification is exact): after the rename the bare names (`In`, `Polynomial`, `Edge`) are shared
       by several enums and types. Foundation's and ModelingData's, renamed first, were qualified where the compiler
       found them ambiguous (about 6,000 references, mechanically from its errors).
1355. **IDE1006 is an error in the build** (`EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`, root .editorconfig), off by folder where the
       code doesn't obey yet: OCCT's names on purpose (NCollection, TCollection, `PackedList`; AdvApp2Var's f2c code);

       of the kernel and the modelling layer with 3,337 violations, mostly 15304's parameters and locals, then type

1356. **The projects and assemblies take Kerf's names**: `Kerf.Kernel.Foundation`, `.ModelingData`,
       `.ModelingAlgorithms`, `.DataExchange` (folders, projects and assemblies), `Kerf.Analyzers`, the tests
