## Phase 10: unit 10H1, the working overlay

1359. **The working overlay** (plan 2.4; `WorkingOverlay`, internal, ModelingData's BRepTools folder). An operation
       opens one at its public entry (`WorkingOverlay.Begin(input, context)`), runs OCCT's in-place code on the caller's
       frozen shape, and ends with `Finish(result, others)`.
       - **Edits are replacements of TShapes.** The first write into a frozen TShape (through `BrepBuilder`'s updates,
         `Builder.Add`/`Remove`, or the TShapes' internal setters and `Change…` lists) makes its working copy: a new
         TShape with its data (`BrepTools.CopyData`: representations copied, geometry shared), flags and children. That
         write and every later one go there. A frozen TShape is never written; unfrozen ones (the operation's own) are
         written in place, as in OCCT.
       - **Reads go through it.** While the overlay is open, a frozen TShape's getters (flags, `ChildCount`, the
         vertex's, edge's and face's data, their `EmptyCopy`) and `TopoDS_Iterator` (so `TopExp_Explorer` and
         `MapShapes`) answer from its working copy. `BRep_Tool` and code reading TShapes directly need no change.
       - **Identity stays the caller's.** Shapes keep the input's TShapes while the operation runs, so `IsSame`, shape
         maps and the operation's ReShape context are keyed by the caller's own sub-shapes: nothing is re-keyed, at the
         entry or the end.
       - **The result shares the rest.** `Finish` walks the result, the shapes in `others` and the context's
         replacements: a frozen TShape with no change below it is itself; a changed one is its working copy (or a copy
         of its data when only its children changed) holding the assembled children; the operation's own TShapes get
         their children replaced in place. A working copy whose data and children equal its original's (a tolerance
         "raised" to its value; the cache bits ignored, as `KeepUnchanged`) gives back the original. Nothing written,
         the input itself.
       - **The history is direct**: `History()` has each of the input's vertices, edges, faces and solids that changed,
         modified into what stands for it now; `Final(s)` maps any shape; `Composed(h)` maps the operation's own history
         (already over the caller's sub-shapes) and adds the in-place changes. In the context, a sub-shape changed
         without a request is recorded as replaced, as `CopyAtEntry` does (decision 643).
       - **Nesting**: an overlay opened inside another sees the outer one's working copies and keeps its own writes; its
         result is its own and the outer state doesn't change.
       - **Threads**: the current overlay is an `AsyncLocal`, so tasks and `Parallel.For` bodies an operation starts
         share it, and operations elsewhere, on the same frozen inputs, have their own. The accessors read it from a
         thread static the `AsyncLocal`'s change handler keeps equal, and skip most lookups with a small filter of the
         written TShapes' hashes. Working copies are made under a lock (a `ConcurrentDictionary` for the reads).
       - **Without an overlay nothing changes**: the same exceptions on writes into frozen shapes
         (`LockedShapeException`, `ImmutableObjectException`), the same reads. When no overlay is open anywhere, an
         accessor costs one more static read; when one is open somewhere, a frozen TShape's accessor also reads a
         thread static (decision 1363's measurements).
       - **Not taken** (overlay-survey.md section 3): code editing `TShape._shapes` itself (17 sites in algorithms) and representations obtained through the read-only `Curves()`/`Points()` of a frozen TShape without a
         working copy, which stay frozen and throw as before (fail fast). 10H2 to 10H6 reroute their modules' sites.
1360. **The context the builder consults, not an explicit builder and tool pair.** Both were prototyped on
       ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance's `LimitTolerance` (`WorkingOverlayPrototypeTests`; they give the same result).
       - **A, an overlay-aware pair** the algorithm calls instead of `BRep_Builder` and `BRep_Tool`: `LimitTolerance`
         needed each of its 6 reads and writes rewritten and the pair passed down. On ShapeFix_Edge, the pilot, the pair
         would have to reach every helper the fixes call: ShapeAnalysis_Edge, ShapeBuild_Edge, ShapeFix_EdgeProjAux,
         ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance, BRepLib's `SameParameter` and BRepAdaptor, about 300 `BRep_Tool`, builder and TShape
         sites in 8 classes; across the engine `BRep_Tool` alone is called at about 6,200 sites. Every helper would
         need an overlay parameter or a second form, and a read missed would silently see the old data.
       - **B, a context consulted by the TShapes, the builder and the iterator**: no edit in the algorithm or its
         helpers; the hooks are in seven files of ModelingData (TShape, BrepTVertex, BrepTEdge, BrepTFace, BrepBuilder's
         29 `Locked()` tests, Builder, Iterator). A missed write still throws, as today. Chosen.
       - The cost of B is process-wide state, which plan 2.7 otherwise removes. It is scoped to one operation and flows
         with its tasks, which a static never did; 10I keeps it.
1361. **Built on `KeepUnchanged`'s machinery, not on ReShape.** The working copies are made with
       `BrepTools.CopyData`/`CopyFlags` (decision 416's exact copy, one TShape at a time) and compared with `IsSameData`
       (`KeepUnchanged`'s test), now internal rather than private; `Finish` is `KeepUnchangedIn` without the copy.
       `BRepTools_ReShape` and `ShapeBuild_ReShape` record replacements of shapes that an algorithm requests and rebuild
       parents when applied; they can't make the algorithm's later reads see an edit, which is what in-place code
       needs. They stay what they are, the algorithms' own contexts, now keyed by the caller's shapes directly
       (15601). `CopyAtEntry`, `ExactCopyForWrite`, `KeepUnchanged…` and `CopyFrozenForWrite` stay until 10H6 removes
       them with the last site.
1362. **The overlay survey** (docs/overlay-survey.md, `tools/overlay-survey.py`): 113 copy-at-entry sites before
       10H1 (Booleans 10, construction 34, healing 38, offsets 5, fillets 2, features 6, other 18), 110 after the
       pilot; 227 frozen-shape checks and markers; the in-place edit kinds with the builder method and TShape member
       each reaches, and how the overlay takes it. It is 10H2 to 10H6's work list, with a recipe (section 6).
1363. **The pilot: ShapeFix_Edge's twins on the overlay**, with ShapeFix_ShapeTolerance's (where the prototypes ran).
       Each twin opens an overlay, runs the in-place fix on the caller's edge and finishes; `CopyAtEntry` is gone from
       both. Level 1: the tests are unchanged, and `The_pilot_gives_what_copy_at_entry_gave` compares six twins with
       the copy-at-entry path value for value (flags, tolerances, ranges, representations, geometry by identity) and
       sharing for sharing. Measured (a fix repeated 2,000 times, Release, one thread):
       - `AddPCurveFixed` (a frozen circle on a frozen cylinder): 7.9 to 18.9 µs and 12.3 KB on a copy; 5.9 to 14.8 µs
         and 9.2 KB on the overlay (allocation −25%).
       - `ToleranceLimited` (a frozen box, every tolerance limited): 24 to 38 µs and 87.8 KB; 25 to 27 µs and 50 KB
         (−43%).
       - `SameParameterFixed` with nothing to do: 3.5 to 4.4 µs and 10.2 KB; 2.4 to 3.0 µs and 7.1 KB (−30%).
       - The ranges are the machine's noise (other units ran beside): the best of 9 rounds, in several runs. On `main`
         the copy path measured the same (18.9 to 19.9 µs, 38 to 42 µs, 5.4 µs).
       - The hooks' cost on reads (a loop of `BRep_Tool` reads and an explorer over a frozen box, 1,000 times): 1.42 to
         1.80 ms on `main`; with the hooks and no overlay open, 1.42 to 2.30 ms, within the noise; with an overlay open on
         another thread, 1.70 to 1.96 ms; inside an overlay holding a working copy, 2.03 to 2.49 ms (about 1.3 times).
1364. **Rules for 10H2 to 10H6** (overlay-survey.md section 6). Open the overlay at the public entry only, run on the
       caller's shape, and pass everything the operation hands out through `Finish` (or `Final`): a generated shape
       left out holds the caller's TShapes without the edits. Histories are kept over the caller's sub-shapes, as
       OCCT keeps them; `Composed` adds the in-place changes. Each unit removes its module's copy-at-entry sites and
       the `// OCCT.NET: frozen` workarounds the overlay makes unnecessary, reroutes its direct `_shapes` and
       read-only-representation edits, and keeps its tests at level 1, or level 2 with a reason. The last (10H6)
       removes `CopyAtEntry`, `ExactCopyForWrite`, `KeepUnchanged…`, `CopyFrozenForWrite`, `HoldsFrozen` and the
       `…Unfrozen`/`…OfFrozen` builder forms; the frozen-shape exceptions stay as long as a write outside an overlay can
       reach a frozen shape.
## Phase 10: unit 10F, errors

1365. **The result types are in Foundation, in the namespace `Kerf`** (10D put them in ModelingData because a
       diagnostic names shapes; the unit's brief asked for Foundation, the lowest assembly, so every engine package can
       return them). `Result<T>`, `Result`, `Diagnostic`, `DiagnosticCode`, `Severity` and `KerfException` are 10D's
       design (README.md section 2), with tests (Foundation.Tests/Results). A diagnostic's shapes, which Foundation
       can't name, are C# 14 extension members from ModelingData (`diagnostic.Shapes`, `diagnostic.WithShapes(…)`,
       class `Kerf.DiagnosticShapes`), stored in an internal field. Additions to 10D's draft: `IsFailure`;
       `Failure(ImmutableArray<Diagnostic>)` for several errors; `Diagnostic.Error`/`Warning` factories and `IsError`;
       `default(Result<T>)` is a failure coded `result.default`; a success can't carry an error and a failure must
       (`ArgumentException`); `KerfException`'s message is the first error's, with how many more there are.
       `Built<TShape>` is in ModelingData with the engine's `History` and `where TShape : struct` until 10L's
       `ShapeHistory` and `IShape<T>` exist. A type in `Kerf` hides a same-named one a file in a `Kerf.*` namespace
       imports (Roslyn's `Diagnostic` in the analyzer tests needed an alias inside the namespace); 10L should avoid
       public names in `Kerf` that the engine or modelling layer import from elsewhere.
1366. **Diagnostic codes are dotted lower-case strings** (decision 1349, 61: "strings, like analyzer IDs", read as
       stable strings rather than an enum; the form is 10D's `boolean.self-interference`, not `KERF1234`):
       words of letters, digits and hyphens, the first the area. `DiagnosticCode` refuses any other form. Four
       bridges make them, each in the assembly of what it reads (docs/api/diagnostics.md has the table):
       `FailureDiagnostics` (Foundation: an OCCT exception is `engine.` plus its class name without the package,
       kebab-cased, `StdFail_NotDone` → `engine.not-done`; any other exception from the engine `engine.fault`;
       `BRepAlgoAPI_Failure` → `boolean.failed`), `AlertDiagnostics` (ModelingData: a report's failures as errors, its
       alarms and warnings as warnings, coded area plus the alert's name, `boolean.self-interfering-shape`, the message
       from OCCT's message table, the alert's shape named), `StatusDiagnostics` and `OperationDiagnostics`
       (ModelingAlgorithms: the construction, loft, fillet, offset and feature status enums by hand-written codes and
       messages; a failed operation's exception or report), `ExchangeDiagnostics` (DataExchange: `IFSelect_ReturnStatus`).
       Codes derived by rule follow OCCT's names, which `OcctTypeNames` keeps; the table is regenerated from the
       bridges when they change.
1367. **The modelling layer's kernel failures say what was being done again** (decision 1342's loss). An internal
       `Failures.Doing(what, operation)` around the kernel calls of the primitives (box, cone, cylinder, sphere,
       torus, wedge), lofts, extrusions (plain, with rotation, tapered, until), revolutions, sweeps, thickening,
       triangulation and every Boolean turns an escaping `FailureException` (or a failed Boolean's report) into a
       `KerfException`: the kernel's diagnostics, each error's message prefixed `box 0.0 × 1.0 × 1.0 failed: `,
       nested operations joined (`extrude until / extrude failed: …`), the kernel's exception as the inner exception.
       It is what `Result<T>.Value` will throw once 10M gives the layer results, and Bento's `#VALUE!` shows the
       message. The Booleans' `ThrowIfFailed` gives the report's alerts as diagnostics (with their shapes) where it
       threw `StdFail_NotDone` naming them. The public signatures are unchanged; the exception type of those
       operations' kernel failures changes from OCCT.NET's to `KerfException`. The layer's best-effort catches that
       caught `FailureException` catch `KerfException` too, so no path changes. Fillets, chamfers and offsets keep
       build123d's own `ArgumentException`/`InvalidOperationException` messages, which already name the operation;
       STEP import keeps its `ArgumentException`, its message now the exchange status's diagnostic, with a
       `KerfException` inside. Tests changed: `ErrorContextTests` (`APrimitiveSaysWhatItWasMaking` and
       `AFeatureSaysWhichItWas` expect `KerfException` and the context, as before 10B; `AFailedBooleanNamesOcctsReasons`
       checks the diagnostics; three new: `ANestedOperationSaysBoth`, `TheLayersOwnErrorsPassThrough`,
       `TheContextIsFormattedOnlyOnFailure`, new names rather than 10B's removed ones), and the catch filters of
       `MalformedInputTests` and `InputsUnchangedTests`. 1,875 tests (1,872 and three).
1368. **Exceptions as statuses, measured** (plan 2.5). A startup hook counted every first-chance exception with its
       stack: Bento's workload throws none (as 9E found); build123d.NET's suite 1,977, of which the kernel's are
       mostly the malformed-BRep tests' own and failing fillets (one per failed stripe, ChFi3d's `StartSol`, a failure
       path); the ModelingAlgorithms suite 38,602, of which 32,869 were one pair: ShapeProcess's
       `ProcessContext.GetBoolean`/`StringVal` reading a parameter with `Resource_Manager.Integer`/`Value` and catching
       its `Standard_NoSuchObject` when the parameter isn't set, which is usual (every operator asks for each option).
       Replaced by `Resource_Manager.TryGetInteger` (new, beside `Integer`) and `Find(name, out value)`: the same
       answers, no exception (0.07 µs a lookup pair against 4 µs; the ShapeProcess, ShapeUpgrade and ShapeCustom tests
       throw 20 exceptions in place of 32,890; the tests' own times are within the machine's noise, 15 to 24 s either
       way). The other pair that fires routinely crosses the boundary:
       build123d.NET's 2D chamfer asked `BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet2d::Modified` about every vertex and untouched edge,
       which throws (OCCT's `DescendantEdge`), and caught it; it now asks `IsModified` first (17 exceptions per two
       chamfers to none; the time is within noise). The 55 catches inside loops that a search found are OCCT's guards
       around a step that may fail (`OCC_CATCH_SIGNALS`), firing only on failure, and stay with the long tail (plan 2.5).
       What remains in the kernel's source: 3,298 `throw` sites of its own exception types and 913 `Raise_if` checks;
       221 catch sites, 109 of OCCT's types and 112 of `Exception` under a filter (`ModelAlgo.IsCaughtFailure`), two
       fewer than before. The modelling layer's own exceptions-as-statuses (`Selector`'s
       measures, 553 per suite) are 10M's.
1369. **How 10L wraps the engine's `Perform`/`IsDone` algorithms** (they stay as they are: the engine, Draw-lite and
       the oracle use them). Each public operation:
       1. checks its arguments first, throwing .NET's argument exceptions for misuse;
       2. builds the engine algorithm, adapts `(IProgress<double>?, CancellationToken)` to a `Message_ProgressRange`,
          and runs it inside a `try` that turns an escaping `FailureException` (or a fault, `ModelAlgo.IsCaughtFailure`'s
          .NET exceptions) into `Result<T>.Failure(OperationDiagnostics.FromException(e))`, and rethrows
          `OperationCanceledException` (a user break is cancellation, not a diagnostic);
       3. reads the algorithm's own account before `Shape()`: not `IsDone` gives the error from its status enum
          (`StatusDiagnostics`), its report (`OperationDiagnostics.FromReport`, with a per-operation fallback error), or
          a per-operation code (`<area>.failed`) when it has neither; it never calls `Shape()` on an algorithm that isn't
          done, which would throw `StdFail_NotDone`;
       4. on success, collects warnings (the report's warnings and alarms, `HasWarnings`) into the success's
          diagnostics, and returns `Built<T>` with the shape and the algorithm's history.
       One shared helper in ModelingAlgorithms should do 2 to 4 for `BRepBuilderAPI_MakeShape` and `BOPAlgo_Options`
       algorithms, so each operation is a few lines. New codes go into diagnostics.md, and those a program will test
       for become static properties on the area's operations class.
## Phase 10: unit 10G, immutability

1370. **gp's public values are `readonly struct`s** (phase10-plan.md 2.2; design-rules.md 3): `Point3D`, `Vector3D`,
       `Direction3D`, `Axis3D`, `Frame3D`, `CoordinateSystem`, `Transform3D`, `GeneralTransform3D`, `Matrix3x3`, the
       conics and quadrics, and their 2D twins (31 types), and `Placement`. Their 438 in-place mutators (`Transform`,
       `SetX`, `Normalize`…) and the three `ref` accessors (`ChangeCoord`, `Matrix3x3.ChangeValue`) are gone; the
       returning forms that already existed (`Transformed`, `WithX`, `Normalized`) are the only way to a changed value.
       - **Callers:** every call outside the type's own declaration, 5,257 in 707 files of the kernel, Draw-lite and the
         tests (none in the modelling layer, which used the returning forms already), became `x = x.Transformed(t);`,
         rewritten by a Roslyn tool from the compiler's symbols (scratch, not committed); `SetLinearForm` became the
         new static `Vector3D.LinearForm`/`Vector2D.LinearForm`. The 93 uses of `ChangeCoord` became a new value of
         the coordinates (`p = new Point3D(p.XYZ() + v)`), the compound expressions kept in brackets.
         Where OCCT built a transformation in two steps (`gp_Trsf T; T.SetRotation(…)`), the 278 pairs
         `T t = new(); t = t.WithRotation(…);` are folded into `T t = new T().WithRotation(…);`.
       - **Inside the types:** each returning form runs its mutator's body on locals copied from the fields it
         changes, and builds the result through a private constructor of all the fields; where a mutator called
         another of its type's own (`Power` calling `Invert`), the locals take the whole value back by deconstruction.
         `Orthogonalize` is a static function of the matrix. Where a public constructor has the private one's
         parameter types and only assigns (`Point3D(Xyz)`), it serves; where it checks (`Circle3D(Frame3D, double)`)
         the check is kept, as the values it sees are valid; `Cone`'s takes its arguments in another order and
         `Frame2D`'s orthogonalizes, so their calls were ordered to match and `Frame2D` keeps a private one;
         `Direction3D`'s private constructor takes a unit vector as it is (`isUnit`), the public one normalizes.
       - **Results are the same to the bit:** a copy runs the same arithmetic as the in-place call. Calls whose argument
         was the receiver itself (`v.SetLinearForm(a, v, b, w)`, `m.Multiply(m)`, 121 of them) were checked: each is
         component-wise or computes into temporaries first, so aliasing never changed a result.
1371. **The engine's scratch structs stay mutable:** `Xyz`, `Xy`, `Matrix2x2`, `Quaternion3` and the interpolators are
       engine types the maths writes in place; KERF0001 still reports a mutation of a read-only copy of them. It now
       allows a readonly struct's constructor to change its own fields (the compiler does), and has a test for it.
1372. **The shapes' value mutators stay internal for 10H:** `Shape`, `Edge`… keep their internal in-place
       `Orientation(o)`, `Location(l)`, `Reverse()`, `Nullify()` (about 1,400 calls). They are topology's, which 10H
       reworks with the overlay, and 10H1 runs beside this unit: rewriting them here would collide with it. They have no
       public mutator, so KERF0003 passes.
1373. **Geometry has no public mutator; its internal ones build fresh objects** (phase10-plan.md 2.4). Geom's and
       Geom2d's classes already had none public (they have 482 public `With…` copies); 384 internal mutators
       remain, each starting with `CheckMutable()`, which throws on a published (frozen) object. Audited with a Roslyn
       pass over their 1,116 calls in the kernel: 188 are a class's own (a mutator through another), 397 on an object
       created by `new` or `Copy()` in the same method, 344 on a local from a converter, builder or copy
       (`CopyBSpline`, `GeomConvert.CurveToBSplineCurve`, `Writable`), 91 on a parameter, 57 on an algorithm's own field,
       39 other. The parameters, fields and others sampled are helpers handed a copy their caller made in the same
       operation (`PutInBounds`, `SegmentCurve`, Gordon's working curves) or guarded by `IsFrozen ? Copy()`; none writes
       into geometry an operation was given. The internal mutators stay as the construction-time half of 2.4's rule ("a
       B-spline is built, then published"); 10L's builders replace them at the public boundary.
1374. **The public geometry's collections are standard read-only lists** (question 50): the 36 `Poles()`, `Knots()`,
       `Weights()`… of `BSplineCurve3D`, `BezierCurve3D`, `BSplineSurface`, `BezierSurface` and the 2D curves return
       `IReadOnlyList<T>` (still a `PackedList`, without copying) in place of Schematiq's `PackedList<T>`. The surfaces'
       `Poles()`/`Weights()` return fresh `NCollection_Array2` copies until 10J's `Grid<T>`.
1375. **KERF0003 fails the build when a public type of a public namespace can be changed** (design-rules.md's
       KERF0101 to KERF0103, as one rule): a public or protected `set` (`init` allowed), a public field not `readonly`, a
       public member of a struct not `readonly`, or a public `void` method named `Set…` or after an in-place operation
       (`Transform`, `Reverse`, `Segment`…), on a public class or struct in `Kerf` or `Kerf.<Area>` (not
       `Kerf.Engine.*`). It runs on the kernel's four assemblies, with tests in Foundation.Tests. Geom's `ResD1` to
       `ResD3`, written through `out` parameters at 630 places, are exempt by `#pragma` until 10L replaces them with
       `CurveDerivatives`.
1376. **Out of 10G's scope, by decision 1349:** STEP's 1,556 entity setters (63: the entities become internal) and
       `InternalsVisibleTo`, which stays between the four kernel assemblies (54); `Placement`'s value equality is 10L's
       (62).
1377. **Performance, measured back to back with main** (9E's benchmarks, Release, on a machine shared with other
       helpers): Bento's examples, median recalculation of nine passes, 1,258 and 1,245 ms on main, 1,275 and 1,233 ms
       after, the same volumes, faces and triangles, and the same allocation to 0.2 MB in each example; the Booleans
       suite's 407 simple cases, serial, 2,256, 2,305 and 3,494 ms on main, 2,408, 2,574, 2,940 and 2,662 ms after, 8.25
       MB per Boolean either way (parallel timings ranged 1.7 to 3.8 s on both, all noise). Copies of the values cost no
       allocation; the Booleans' serial medians differ by about 13%, inside the machine's spread but on the slow side
       in every run after, so 10J should profile the transforms' returning forms (`Transform3D` is 112 bytes, and its
       forms copy every field) when it measures with 9E's benchmarks on a quiet machine.

## Phase 10: unit 10H2, no copy at entry in the Booleans

1378. **The general fuse keeps OCCT's non-destructive mode, asked of the overlay.** The pave filler, the builders,
       the splitter, sections, cells and `BRepAlgoAPI_*` never copied at entry: frozen arguments are locked, which
       turns OCCT's own non-destructive mode on (decisions 577, 1056), and the result shares every argument sub-shape it
       didn't change. That stays: opening an overlay at their public entry would make every Boolean destructive and
       change results that native's non-destructive runs pinned. `SetNonDestructive` now asks what OCCT's `Locked()`
       means, whether a write would be refused: `WorkingOverlay.IsLocked` on the argument, and outside an overlay any
       frozen sub-shape (decision 1056's walk, now `HoldsLocked`, in place of `BrepTools.HoldsFrozen`). Inside an
       operation's overlay a frozen argument takes writes, so a Boolean that the operation runs (the periodicity's trim
       and gluing) is destructive, as OCCT's on an unlocked shape: the same results the copies gave, since they were
       unfrozen. Outside an overlay nothing changes.
1379. **The Booleans' copy-at-entry sites run in working overlays** (overlay-survey.md section 6), all 14 of them:
       - `BOPAlgo_CheckerSI`: the check runs on the argument in an overlay that takes the filler's stray tolerance
         writes (`PutPaveOnCurve`, occt-issues.md) and is dropped unfinished: the checker hands out no shape built from
         them. The data structure holds the argument's own sub-shapes, so `Original` is gone, and with it the mapping in
         `BOPAlgo_ArgumentAnalyzer` and Draw-lite's `bopcheck`.
       - `BOPAlgo_Tools::WiresToFaces`, `BRepAlgo::ConcatenateWireC0`, `BRepAlgo_FaceRestrictor::Perform`,
         `TopOpeBRepBuild_WireToFace::MakeFaces` (decision 793): OCCT's code on the caller's wires, the faces or edge
         handed out through `Finish`/`Final`. `WireToFace.HolderOf`, the Booleans' one direct `_shapes` edit, is gone:
         an overlay may now be opened without an input (15703).
       - `BOPAlgo_CellsBuilder::AddToResult`: a published result takes new parts in an overlay (`UnfreezeResult` is
         gone); the next result is a new compound holding the old parts and the new.
       - `BOPAlgo_RemoveFeatures`' `RemoveInternalWires`: OCCT's in-place removal again, in an overlay, in place of the
         frozen-face copies and `ReplaceFaces`; the faces it replaced are recorded as before.
       - `BOPAlgo_MakePeriodic`: the trim (a Common) and the gluing of the repetitions run in overlays in place of
         `CopyFrozenForWrite`. At each end the periodic, repeated and input shapes are what stands for them, the
         histories are merged with the overlay's images, and the twins mapped. `BOPAlgo_MakeConnected` no longer copies
         the connected shape: it reads it back from the tool, and brings the gluing history up to date with the
         sub-shapes the tool changed in place when the shape is made periodic again.
1380. **Two additions to `WorkingOverlay`.** `Begin` takes a null input, for an operation on several shapes that keeps
       no history over them (the wire tools: what they hand out goes through `Finish`'s others and `Final`).
       `Images(shapes)` gives, after `Finish`, each of the given shapes (mapped before `Finish`, as placed) whose TShape
       was replaced, modified into what stands for it: merged into a history kept over the operation's own shapes
       (translated copies, glued results), it brings that history up to date, as `Composed` does for one over the
       input's sub-shapes.
1381. **Histories are direct.** The periodicity's and the connected shape's histories record a sub-shape as modified
       only when it changed (natively it is the same shape, changed in place); with the copies every frozen sub-shape was
       "modified" into its copy. A shape that is an initial shape of the history with only generated shapes (the
       repetitions' `AddGenerated(s, s)`) is modified into what stands for it. `BOPAlgo_ConnectedNativeTests` (126
       cases, 499 steps, published and unpublished) still match native's recordings in every step, within the categories the test accepts (identical, Free
       masked, history as sets, twins order, in-place); no test moved to level 2.
1382. **The tests**: `BooleanInputsUnchangedTests` checks after each kind (fuse, cut, common, section, splitter,
       general fuse, cells, the checks, defeaturing, connected and periodic shapes, the wire tools) that the arguments
       are unchanged TShape for TShape and value for value (`ShapeSnapshot`), and that the result holds the arguments'
       own sub-shapes where the operation didn't change them. Defeaturing's faces are still copies where
       UnifySameDomain adds p-curves (healing's copy at entry, 10H4).
1383. **The survey recounted** (overlay-survey.md): `tools/overlay-survey.py` missed the target-typed constructor
       (`CopyAtEntry entry = new(input)`); with it 119 sites were left after 10H1 (Booleans 14, construction 38,
       features 7, not 10, 34 and 6). After 10H2: 105, none in the Booleans; frozen-shape checks 221 (Booleans 2, the
       pave filler's own). The `_shapes` sites BOPTools' `ConnexityBlock` and `ToolSet` show are those classes' fields,
       not a TShape's.
1384. **Measured** (`benchmarks/Kerf.Kernel.Benchmarks -- booleans`, Release, back to back on a shared machine):
       Allocation is unchanged, 11.92 MB per Boolean on the complex grid (193 cases) and
       8.25 to 8.26 MB on the simple (407): the general fuse never copied, and its one change (the locking walk asks
       the overlay) costs what `HoldsFrozen` did. Serial time 2,989 ms before and 2,541 ms after on the complex grid,
       3,288 and 3,114 ms on the simple; parallel 1,996 and 1,675 ms, 2,564 and 2,286 ms: the differences are the
       machine's noise (other units ran beside), not the change. The converted sites (the checks, the wire tools,
       cells, defeaturing's wires, the periodicity) are outside the benchmark; each now copies only the TShapes it
       writes, where it copied the whole input (10H1's pilot measured 25 to 43% less allocation for that change).

## Phase 10: unit 10I, state

1385. **One operation context, ambient** (plan 2.7; docs/state.md). `Kerf.Engine.Foundation.OperationContext`
       (Foundation, `Context/`) holds the settings OCCT kept in process-wide statics. A setting is a `ContextKey<T>`,
       a name and an immutable default, declared `static readonly` by the class it configures, so Foundation knows none
       of the other assemblies' settings. A context is immutable (`With`, `Without`) and overrides few settings, kept as
       key and value pairs scanned by identity. The current one is an `AsyncLocal`: it flows into the tasks and
       `Parallel.For` bodies an operation starts and into the operations nested in it, and other flows (threads,
       tests, Bento's cells) see their own. `Begin(…)` sets a scope, restored on disposal; `Set(key, value)` changes
       the setting for the rest of the current flow and is what OCCT's process-wide setters now do
       (`Quantity_Color::SetEpsilon`, `BOPAlgo_Options::SetParallelMode`, `GeomTools::SetUndefinedTypeHandler`,
       `ShapeAlgo::SetAlgoContainer`, `Message::SetDefaultMessenger`, BRepLib's `Precision`/`Plane`,
       `BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh::SetParallelDefault`, `BRepMesh_DiscretFactory::SetDefaultName`, AppBlend's and Blend's
       debug switches). Where nothing was set, a read is one `AsyncLocal` read. The setters were internal or used only by
       Draw-lite and tests, whose commands run synchronously, so a setting still lasts for the rest of a command
       sequence, but no longer reaches another test or interpreter running beside it.
1386. **Ambient where the chain is long, parameters where it is short.** The settings are read deep in OCCT's call
       graph (the message table by every algorithm that reports, BRepLib's plane by the 2D makers, the mesher's
       defaults by every factory call), where a parameter would touch hundreds of signatures. What already travels
       explicitly stays explicit: a `ProcessContext` carries its resource manager, an algorithm its own
       `SetRunParallel`, a STEP session its parameter set (decision 1222). Rejected: one context object passed down,
       which is the parameter threading by another name.
1387. **What the context doesn't hold.** 10H1's working overlay keeps its own `AsyncLocal`, mirrored in the thread
       static its accessors read on every TShape access (decision 1359): it flows the same way, and folding it in would
       add an indirection to that hot path while 10H2 changes it. No scratch pools: an operation's parallel bodies run
       on several threads, so per-operation scratch would race; the scratch OCCT keeps across calls stays per thread
       where that is OCCT's own scope (`thread_local`) and a new instance always starts afresh, so nothing crosses
       operations: BlendFunc_ConstRad's and EvolRad's values (decision 1037), Contap_HContTool's sampling bounds
       (1075), TopOpeBRepTool's classifier, GeomTools' reading depth, AdvApp2Var's Hermite cache (113).
1388. **The message table, ShapeProcess's registry and `Resource_Manager`: immutable defaults, overrides per flow.**
       - `MsgFile`: the compiled-in texts (BOPAlgo's, SHMessage's, XSMessage's) go into an immutable default table
         once each, through their owners' `Lazy` initialisations (`AddDefaults`), the table replaced by
         compare-and-swap so readers take no lock; `AddMsg`/`LoadFromString` (internal: Draw-lite and tests) add to the
         flow (`AdditionsSetting`). `Msg` of an unknown keyword no longer stores OCCT's surrogate text under it: a read
         wrote the process's table, and `AlertDiagnostics` (which asks `HasMsg` first) gave a later operation another
         message for an alert an earlier one had looked up. `MsgFile_UnknownKeyword` now expects `HasMsg` false after.
       - ShapeProcess: `OperLibrary.Init` publishes the 18 operators once as a frozen dictionary; `RegisterOperator`
         adds to the flow (`OperatorsSetting`), refusing a name either layer has, as OCCT refuses a second registration.
       - `ProcessContext.LoadResourceManager`: OCCT's cache of the last file, five statics behind a mutex reloaded on a
         new name or modification time, goes. A compiled-in file is parsed once per name (a `ConcurrentDictionary`,
         invisible: each context gets a copy); the caller's directories are read each time. New:
         `ProcessContext.ResourceOverridesSetting`, resources by full name applied to every context loaded in the flow,
         the STEP and IGES readers' included, so an operation can run with its own shape processing parameters beside
         others on the defaults. `ClearResourceCache` (Draw-lite's corpus) goes with the cache.
1389. **State that crossed operations is the operation's own.**
       - BRepAlgo_Image's `Image` of a shape without images appends it to a list OCCT keeps static and returns, and
         BRepAlgo_AsDes hands out a static "empty" list `ChangeDescendant` can fill (both `// OCCT`). They were per
         thread, so one offset's appends reached the next offset on that thread; they are now the object's own, which
         keeps OCCT's behaviour within an operation. No test changed.
       - STEPConstruct_Assembly's `MakeRelationship()` numbered occurrences from a process-wide counter; nothing called
         it (the writer passes its own counter, decision 1266), so it is removed.
       - Removed as unread: HLRBRep_Data's seven intersection counters (written unsynchronised from the hider, read
         only by OCCT's `OCCT_DEBUG` traces) and AdvApp2Var's common block `mblank__` (written by `macinit_`, never read).
       - One-time initialisations are `Lazy<T>` or static initialisers: BOPAlgo's, Shape Healing's and data exchange's
         messages, ShapeProcess's operators, ShapeAlgo's container, the STEP and STEP-XCAF controllers, and the mesh
         factory registry (built in `DiscretAlgoFactory`'s static initialiser from the two factories, OCCT's
         self-registering singletons gone; `RegisterFactory`/`UnregisterFactory` act only on the registry being built).
1390. **Caches stay where invisible, without locks.** Poly_Triangulation's cached range publishes a new box each time
       (never changed once published), so its four locks go; FEmTool's linear criteria (three classes) and an XDE
       assembly's compound publish their first value by compare-and-swap (computed twice at worst, equal); the
       controllers' dictionary is an immutable one replaced by compare-and-swap. `FailureDiagnostics`' codes, the
       streams' `ConditionalWeakTable`s and PLib_HermitJacobi's matrices were lock-free already.
1391. **The locks left** (docs/state.md lists them): the writer locks of LibCtl's global lists and StepData's header
       protocol, reached only from the protocols' one-time initialisations; the locks of one operation's own objects
       written by its parallel bodies (BVH's build queue, Message_Report, the progress range, the overlay, DistanceShapeShape's
       inner-solid search, StepSelect_StepType's library, the modelling layer's warning scope); the shape log's file
       (test tooling, off by default); and `XSControl_WorkSession`'s, which was OCCT's process-wide mutex around
       `NewModel` and `TransferWriteShape` and is now the controller's (`Controller.SessionLock`): sessions sharing a
       recorded controller take turns as before, and every STEP reader and writer, which has its own controller
       (decision 1264), waits for no other (`SelectNorm` changes only its session and takes none). One static lock
       remains in an algorithm: BOPAlgo_PaveFiller's `VerticesLock` (decision 789), within one Boolean's parallel
       p-curve makers but shared by Booleans running at once; it is 10H2's file, and the filler can own it there.
1392. **Measured** (Release, 24 logical processors, other units running beside: the figures carry the machine's noise).
       No cost found: the settings read where nothing was set are one `AsyncLocal` read, and the locks removed were
       rarely contended.
       - Bento's benchmark (`Kerf.Kernel.Bento.Benchmarks`, 11 examples, 7 passes; it gains parallel rounds, every
         example 24 times at once on the thread pool, each result checked against the serial one): serial medians
         1,545 ms before, 1,469 ms after; allocation per example unchanged (802 MB for the largest); a parallel round
         11.6 s before, 10.7 s after, 27.7 GB allocated either way, no result differing. The parallel rounds are
         dominated by workstation GC (23 to 25 s of pauses), not by contention.
       - The Booleans benchmark (`-- booleans simple`, 407 cases): serial 2,651 ms before, 2,693 ms after; parallel
         3,030 ms before (a noisy run), 1,993 ms after; 8.25 MB per Boolean either way.
       - Tests: Foundation 2,272 (2,268 and OperationContextTests' 4), ModelingData 3,145, ModelingAlgorithms 4,736
         (9 skipped), DataExchange 274 (271 and ConcurrencyTests' 3; 1 skipped), Oracle 383, Draw-lite 687, the
         modelling layer 1,876 (1,875 and ConcurrentPartsTests). Changed: `MsgFile_UnknownKeyword` (decision 1388) and
         the Draw-lite meshing test, which reads `mpparallel`'s setting from the interpreter's context.
         Draw-lite's cheap-gaps class failed in two later runs on `bug24157_5`/`_8`'s check that `bbuild -t` takes at
         most 15 s of wall time: alone they take 1 to 3 s; twelve at once take 10 to 12 s, on `main` as on this branch
         (measured both ways); with the class's other cases and other units' suites beside, 18 to 21 s. A timing check
         under load, not a regression; it passed in the first full run.

## Phase 10: unit 10H4, no copy at entry in healing

1393. **Healing's copy-at-entry sites run in working overlays** (overlay-survey.md section 6), 34 of the 35: ShapeFix
       (Shape, Solid, Shell, Face, Wire, WireVertex, Wireframe, FixSmallFace, FreeBounds, ComposeShell, the connect
       fixers, the statics' twins), ShapeBuild_Edge's and ShapeConstruct's twins, ShapeUpgrade's dividers and
       UnifySameDomain, ShapeProcess's context and its modifiers, and sewing. Each runs OCCT's in-place code on the
       caller's shapes; the copies' re-keying goes with the copies (ShapeFix_Shape's fixed-shape keys, UnifySameDomain's
       kept shapes, the context's `Working`/`Copied`, sewing's `ToWork`/`FromWork` maps, the connect fixers' recorded
       shapes, ShapeFix_Wire's Free flags). ShapeContext's `RecModif` is OCCT's again, and its re-copy when an operator
       published the result (`InternalEnsureWritable`) goes: the overlay takes writes into frozen shapes. ShapeFix_Face's
       `Add` adds the wire to the loaded face in the overlay, as OCCT adds it to the caller's, in place of a shallow copy
       (a direct `_shapes` edit). The one site left is `OperLibrary`'s `HoldsFrozen`, asked only outside an overlay
       (decision 1396). The modelling layer's three private copies before ShapeFix (`Fix`, the 2D chamfer, `FixDegenerateEdges`)
       go too.
1394. **Three ways in, by what the tool is.**
       - **One call, OCCT-shaped** (ShapeFix_Shape/Solid/Shell's `Perform`, `UnifySameDomain.Build`, the dividers'
         `Perform`, ShapeProcess's run of operators, sewing's `Perform`, the free-bounds fixer): an overlay of its own,
         unless one that takes writes is open here (`WorkingOverlay.BeginUnlessWriting`). Then the tool runs in place in
         that one, as OCCT's in-place tools write into the shapes the tool that called them works on: ShapeFix_Shape →
         Solid → Shell → Face → Wire, ShapeProcess → ShapeFix, the dividers → ComposeShell, all in the outermost
         overlay, as they were all on one copy. A nested overlay would keep each inner tool's writes from the outer one.
       - **Several public calls** (a load, fixes one by one, a result: ShapeFix_Face, _Wire, _WireVertex, _Wireframe,
         _FixSmallFace, _ComposeShell): an overlay kept from the first fix to the public result, current only inside each
         call (`WorkingOverlay.Detached`, `Enter`; `ForTool` borrows the current one instead, which the tool then doesn't
         finish). Leaving an overlay open between calls would let a caller's own writes into frozen shapes pass silently,
         and leak if the result were never asked for. The cost: between a fix and the result the tool's shapes show
         the changes only to its fixes (the edges of ShapeFix_Wire's `WireData()`, FixSmallFace's returned shapes); the
         results are as before.
       - **Functional twins** (`…Fixed`, `SameParametered`, `RangesCopied`, `PCurvesJoined`, `Built`, the connect
         fixers' `Build`): always their own overlay (nested if one is open), as 10H1's pilot, now with a caller's
         unfrozen TShapes (a compound built to hold frozen edges) copied first (`WithUnfrozenCopied`) and given back where
         left equal (`UncopiedWhereUnchanged`), so a twin never writes into a caller's shape, frozen or not. The pilot's
         twins take the same step.
1395. **The overlay, two fixes and its additions.** `Finish` maps the input's sub-shapes before it assembles: an
       unfrozen input (a Boolean's result, which `SimplifyResult` unifies) has its children replaced in place by the
       assembly, and mapped afterwards it no longer held the sub-shapes that changed, so `Composed` lost them
       (BRepAlgoAPI's simplified history and six defeaturing histories differed from native). Added: `Writing`,
       `BeginUnlessWriting`, `Detached`, `ForTool`, `Enter` and its `Scope`, `Initial` (the inverse of `Final`, for a
       tool's queries keyed by the shapes it worked with: sewing's sections), `IsReadOnly`, `WithUnfrozenCopied`,
       `CopiedIn`, `UncopiedWhereUnchanged` (`WorkingOverlay.Tools.cs`). A detached overlay is counted open only inside
       its `Enter` scopes and needs no disposal.
1396. **A frozen check that refuses a write asks `WorkingOverlay.IsReadOnly`** (frozen, and no overlay here takes
       writes), not `IsFrozen`: inside an overlay the frozen input stands where the copy stood, and the write goes
       where OCCT's does. ShapeBuild_Edge's and ShapeConstruct's exception filters, ShapeFix_EdgeProjAux's reversed
       pcurve, ShapeFix_Solid's Free flags, `BRepTools::Update(face)`, and BRepLib's SameParameter, which edits the
       representations it reads through `Curves()`: in an overlay it takes them through `ChangeCurves()`, the working
       copy's (sewing POINT-TANK.brep gave lines where native gives the approximated pcurves; now identical).
       `OperLibrary` runs the modifiers in the mutable-input mode inside an overlay. Left as they are, outside healing
       or harmless: BRepLib's no-op tolerance write on a frozen vertex, `BRep_Tool::Range`'s Modified flag, the
       modifier's flags, LibraryMakeWire's vertex choices (construction, 10H3).
1397. **The tests stay at level 1.** Every suite keeps its counts and results; no test moved to level 2, and the
       Draw-lite healing groups' cases (heal, sewing, shape upgrade and divide, shape processing, defeaturing) have the
       same statuses case by case. One test changed because it tested the copy, not a result:
       `LoadWireData_WithFrozenEdges_IsCopiedAtTheFirstFix` is `…_IsFixedInAWorkingOverlay` (the wire data holds the
       caller's frozen edges between the fixes). New: `HealingInputsUnchangedTests` (15 cases: ShapeFix_Shape on four
       of OCCT's heal-group inputs, the shell, solid, face, wire and vertex fixers on every sub-shape of one, the
       wireframe, small-face, free-bounds and connect fixers, sewing, UnifySameDomain, the dividers, the twins, every
       ShapeProcess operator on two inputs, and no overlay left open after a tool's calls) and
       `StepHealingInputsUnchangedTests` (STEP import's "FromSTEP" sequence on a frozen imported shape), each checking
       the input untouched (`ShapeSnapshot`), the result frozen, and sub-shapes or geometry shared. The modelling layer's
       `clean` and `fix` cases already check its inputs. UnifySameDomain still makes new faces where it adds p-curves
       to their edges (decision 1382's defeaturing face): a face holding a changed edge is a changed face.
1398. **Measured** (Release, serial, one machine shared with other units: the times carry its noise). The new
       `Kerf.Kernel.Benchmarks -- healing` reads the dataset's 289 STEP files up to 400 kB, then runs ShapeFix_Shape and
       UnifySameDomain on each imported (frozen) shape, the fastest of three runs each; before is `main` at 4052982b.
       - Allocation: STEP import with its healing 6,519 MB before, 6,431 MB after (−1.4%); ShapeFix_Shape 5,548 MB,
         5,365 MB (−3.3%); UnifySameDomain 1,569 MB, 1,364 MB (−13%): each now writes working copies of the TShapes it
         changes, where it copied the whole input.
       - Time: 9,043, 4,614 and 1,185 ms before; 10,852, 5,742 and 1,316 ms in one run after and 8,295, 4,678 and
         1,029 ms in another: within the machine's noise.
       - Bento's benchmark (11 examples, 7 passes): the same results; allocation per example the same or lower (the
         working point 5.8 to 5.4 MB, nesting locations 36.2 to 33.0, the for-loops 22.0 to 20.1 and 17.1 to 15.7, the
         largest 802 MB either way); median recalculation 1,546 ms before, 1,646 and 1,301 ms in two runs after.
       - Tests: ModelingAlgorithms 4,763 (4,748 and the 15 new; 9 skipped), DataExchange 276 (2 new; 1 skipped),
         ModelingData 3,145, Oracle 383, the modelling layer 1,876, Draw-lite's healing classes 23 (every case's status
         as before).
1399. **The survey recounted** (overlay-survey.md): copy at entry 105 → 71 sites (healing 35 → 1); frozen-shape checks
       221 → 187 (healing 83 → 45: the copy's markers gone, the write checks asking `IsReadOnly`); healing's direct
       `_shapes` edits 8 → 4, the four left filling compounds its tools make. Section 7 records 10H4's patterns for
       10H5 and 10H6.
## Phase 10: unit 10J, heap and collections

1400. **10G's Booleans slowdown is not there to fix** (decision 1377 asked 10J to profile it). An EventPipe profile of
       the Booleans benchmark (`-- booleans simple`, 407 cases) puts everything to do with transforms
       (`Transform3D`'s returning forms, `Point3D.Transformed`, `Placement.Transformation`, the transformed adaptors) at
       under 0.5% of the samples: the hot paths already take `in` parameters (3 by-value `Transform3D`/`Matrix3x3`
       parameters remain, none hot), and the returning forms are called when transforms are built, not per point.
       Measured back to back, the commits either side of 10G's merge (296531cd, 348b565a), three runs each alternating:
       serial 2,864, 2,671, 2,879 ms before and 3,380, 2,722, 2,655 ms after, 8.25 MB per Boolean either way. The 13%
       was the machine's noise. The profile's real hot spots were elsewhere, and 1401 to 1404 take them.
1401. **A TShape draws its hash once** (performance.md's proposal 7): `TShape._hash`, from `Random.Shared` at
       construction, is the shapes' hash and the overlay's filter bit, in place of
       `RuntimeHelpers.GetHashCode`, whose slow path was 4.5% of the Booleans' samples. No result depends on it: the
       maps are .NET's hash tables, which iterate in insertion order whatever the hashes (the check proposal 7
       asked for), and nothing sorts or prints by a shape's hash (BRep dumps still print the identity hash). Placement's datums keep their identity hash (not hot).
1402. **KERF0002 matched nothing since the rename.** It looked for `Occt.TopoDS_Shape` and its subtypes; since 10E the
       shapes are `Kerf.Topology.Shape`, `Edge`… It now looks for those, its tests use Kerf's names, and a probe confirms
       it fails the build on `new HashSet<Edge>()`. The kernel, the tests and the modelling layer had no violation.
1403. **The mesher's circles are a `List<int>`** (proposal 3, without a linked list): `BRepMesh_CircleTool.Select` and
       its inspector return the tool's own `List<int>`, and `BRepMesh_Delaun::createTrianglesOnNewVertices` overwrites
       a deleted triangle's entry with a marker rather than removing it, so the rest are visited in OCCT's order without
       being moved (the `List.RemoveAt` that was 7% of meshing in 9E's profile). The phase-10 plan's linked list "only
       where an algorithm splices" isn't needed here: a marker does it.
1404. **Small fixed-size arrays and reused solvers** (plan 2.6's small maths, chosen by the profiles):
       - `Extrema_ExtElC` and `Extrema_ExtElC2d` hold their squared distances and point pairs in `[InlineArray]`
         fields, `_point[2 * i + j]` for OCCT's `myPoint[i][j]`, in place of a `double[]` and a rectangular
         `POnCurv[,]` per object (`Array.CreateInstanceMDArray` was 1.7% of the Booleans' samples).
       - `math_NewtonMinimum` keeps its `math_Jacobi` and `math_Gauss` across iterations and calls (proposal 4),
         through new internal `Jacobi(int n)`/`Perform(Matrix)` and `Gauss(int n)`/`Perform(Matrix, double)`, which hold
         `math_Recipes`' work vectors too (`Jacobi`'s b and z, `LU_Decompose`'s vv). Each run overwrites all of its
         storage, so the arithmetic is the same to the bit.
       - Not done, in collections-plan.md: `math_VectorBase` over its own array, span scratch in `math_Recipes` and
         `math_FunctionSetRoot` (built per `Extrema_GenLocateExtPS.Perform`).
1405. **`Grid<T>`** (docs/api/README.md section 6; decision 1374): a read-only struct in `Kerf.Geometry` over row-major
       `ReadOnlyMemory<T>`, with `RowCount`, `ColumnCount`, `this[row, column]` (0-based, checked), `Row`, `Values` and
       `ToArray`. `BSplineSurface` and `BezierSurface` return their `Poles()`, `Weights()` and `WeightsArray()` as grids
       (copies, rows in U); OCCT's deprecated copy-into overloads `Poles(array)`/`Weights(array)` are internal. The
       engine's two readers use `InternalPoles()`; the tests read the grids 0-based. Their public constructors still
       take `NCollection_Array2` (10L's builders take grids).
1406. **`NCollection_Map` is `HashSet<T>`** (plan 2.6, the first NCollection class to go). The wrapper added only OCCT's
       names over a `HashSet`, so iteration order and results are the same by construction. A Roslyn rewrite from the
       compiler's symbols (scratch) changed 178 files, 1,011 edits, kernel, tests, benchmarks and the modelling layer:
       the type, `Extent()`/`Size()` to `Count`, `IsEmpty()` to `Count == 0` (or `!= 0` under a `!`), and the copy
       constructor to `new HashSet<T>(other, other.Comparer)`, keeping the comparer (KERF0002's exemption for
       NCollection copies doesn't cover `HashSet`). The one `Exchange` (a test) swaps the references. The 9E
       profile's other types follow in collections-plan.md's order.
1407. **The constant tables 10I left as NCollection types are frozen:** STEP AP214's type-name and short-name tables
       (`FrozenDictionary<string, int>`, ordinal), its protocol's type numbers (`FrozenDictionary<Type, int>`, built by
       a static initialiser in place of the static constructor's binds) and MoniTool's typed-value library (a frozen
       dictionary and its names in OCCT's order, which `LibList` returns). The shared static "empty" lists and the
       Bézier classes' shared knot arrays are left (collections-plan.md).
1408. **Step 2 doesn't fit in one unit** (the brief's fallback): about 25,000 references to the NCollection types
       (collections-plan.md counts them per type). 10J did the measured hot spots, one whole type (1406), the returned
       grids and the constant tables; collections-plan.md orders the rest (DataMap, DynamicArray, the indexed maps with
       one small ordered type each, List, Sequence, the arrays, the math vectors), with the design of the indexed maps'
       replacement (`IndexedSet<T>`, `IndexedMap<TKey, TValue>`, 0-based, OCCT's swap-with-last removal; .NET 9's
       `OrderedDictionary` rejected because its removal shifts). Question 55's transient base goes with the arrays.
1409. **Measured** (Release, back to back with `main` at 4052982b, two alternating runs each, on a machine shared with
       other units, so timings carry up to 30% noise):
       - **Bento's benchmark** (11 examples, 7 passes, parallel rounds of 24 copies): "extrude until" allocates
         **142 MB a recalculation, against 802 MB** (−82%: `math_NewtonMinimum`'s solvers, 1404); the other ten
         examples allocate as before (within 1 MB). A parallel round allocates **11.8 GB against 27.7 GB**, with 2,600
         gen-0 collections against 5,900. Median recalculation 1,402 and 2,121 ms after (the second under a load
         spike), 1,396 and 1,375 ms before; "extrude until" 888 and 1,199 ms after, 926 and 919 ms before; parallel
         rounds 8.8 and 7.4 s after, 10.0 and 8.5 s before. Every example gives the same volume, faces and triangles.
       - **The Booleans** (`-- booleans simple`, 407 cases): serial 3,220 and 2,670 ms after, 2,829 and 2,844 ms before;
         parallel 2,922 and 3,474 ms after, 2,182 and 3,515 ms before; 8.25 MB per Boolean either way. The hash and the
         inline arrays remove work the profile saw (6% of its samples) but the difference is inside this machine's noise.
       - **The modelling layer's suite** (`dotnet test`, 1,876 tests): 19 and 23 s before, 23 and 26 s after (noise).
       - **Tests**, all passing with their counts: Foundation 2,297 (2,292 before, and 10J's 5: Grid's 4 and KERF0002's
         new case), ModelingData 3,145, ModelingAlgorithms 4,739 (9 skipped), DataExchange 273 (1 skipped), Oracle
         383, Draw-lite 687, the modelling layer 1,876. No comparison moved to level 2: no result changed.
## Phase 10: unit 10H3, no copy at entry in construction

1410. **Construction runs in working overlays** (overlay-survey.md section 6), all 38 of its copy-at-entry sites:
       - **Sweeps** (`BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism`, `BRepPrimAPI_MakeRevol`, `BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe`, through
         `BRepPrimAPI_MakeSweep`): the generating shape is swept as it is, in an overlay opened in the constructor and
         finished by `Build`, in place of `ExactCopyForWrite` and `KeepUnchangedIn` (decisions 468, 910). The sweep's
         tables are keyed by the caller's sub-shapes, so `ToSwept` goes; what the sweep hands out (first and last shapes,
         the history, MakeRevol's degenerated edges, now mapped too) goes through `Final`.
       - **Lofts** (`BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections`, `BRepFill_Generator`; decisions 936, 937), **ruled faces and shells**
         (`BRepFill::Face`, `BRepFill::Shell`; 897), **evolved shapes** (`BRepFill_Evolved`, `BRepFill_AdvancedEvolved`;
         642 to 644, 1047): OCCT's code on the caller's sections, spine and profile; the result, the first and last
         faces, the generated lists and the working sections are finished together. The maps keyed by copies, and
         `Working`/`Copied`/`Original`, go. A point section (`AddVertex`) of a caller's vertex is frozen with it: it is
         the caller's, and `Wires()` hands it out as given (bugs/modalg_6/bug26150_5, _7, _17 found it).
       - **BRepLib's functional twins** (`TolerancesUpdated`, `SameParametered`, `Curves3dBuilt`, `RegularityEncoded`,
         `DeflectionUpdated`, `NormalConsistencyEnsured`, `InnerTolerancesUpdated`): the in-place static on the input in
         its own overlay. `SameParameter` of an edge used in place asks the edge's representations with `ChangeCurves()`
         when an overlay takes the write (it read the frozen list and edited it, which threw).
       - **The makers**: `BRepLib_MakeFace` from a planar wire (decision 417's copy), `BRepLib_MakeWire`'s merges
         (1413), and the changes of a published result (decisions 414, 455): `UnfreezeResult` goes; MakeFace's,
         MakeSolid's and MakePolygon's `Add`/`Close` on a frozen result run in an overlay (`BeginResultChange`), whose
         working copy is the new result, so the shape handed out never changes.
       - **`BRepProj_Projection`**: its `HoldsFrozen` test goes. The pave filler already finds the caller's frozen faces
         below the new compound and sections non-destructively (decision 1378), as the test made it.
       - **`BRepSweep`'s `UpdateVertexOfFrozen`** (decision 981's second part) goes, and BRep_Builder's form with it:
         `SetDirectingParameter` is OCCT's `UpdateVertex` again. The history builds on demand, after the result is
         published, the edge a vertex generates when no face built it; MakePrism's and MakeRevol's `Generated` now run in
         an overlay dropped unfinished (`BeginQuery`), so that write, which would leave the vertex as it is, goes nowhere.
         The sweep's `Closed` write on a wire it hands out again is made only where a write is taken
         (`!WorkingOverlay.IsLocked`): after the overlay, the caller's wire keeps its flag, and the result holds the
         wire as the sweep left it.
1411. **An algorithm another operation runs writes into that operation's overlay.** `WorkingOverlay.BeginUnlessInside`
       opens an overlay unless an unfinished one is current, and then returns null: the sweeps, the generator, the
       loft, the ruled faces, the evolved shapes, MakeFace's wire and MakeWire's merges run that way. OCCT writes in
       place, and the calling operation reads the writes back (the loft reads its generator's pcurves, the evolved
       shape its sweeps' and pipes') and assembles them into its own result. The copies gave the same: an operation's
       copies were unfrozen, so the algorithms it ran wrote into them in place. Nested overlays (decision 1359) would
       have given each sweep its own copies of the profile's edges. The functional twins and a published result's
       change keep their own overlay: what they return they assemble themselves.
1412. **`WorkingOverlay`'s additions**: `BeginUnlessInside` (1411); `TakesWrite`, for setters that skip a write of the
       value already held (1417); `Finish`'s `ignoreToleranceGuard`, `KeepUnchanged`'s
       (MakeFace's `UpdateTolerances` raises every vertex by its rounding guard, `2 * Epsilon(tol)`, which would
       otherwise replace every vertex of the wire); a child replaced in an operation's own TShape has its Free flag
       cleared, as `TopoDS_Builder::Add` clears it and the copies had it. The working copies' dictionary, the filter and
       the history are made at the first write: an overlay nothing writes into (most makers' changes, a sweep of a
       polygon face) costs an object and the `AsyncLocal`'s two changes.
1413. **MakeWire merges in an overlay** (decision 417's copies go). A change (`Add` of an edge, of a list) runs in one
       when the wire is published, or when the edge has a vertex that isn't one of the wire's (it may be merged); OCCT's
       code is back (`UpdateVertex` of the wire's vertex, `Transfert`, CreateNewVertices' update), without
       `NeedsWritableVertices`, `CopyForWrite` or the frozen `Transfert`. At the end the wire holds new TShapes for what
       changed and the caller's own for the rest, the maker's state (its vertices, VF, VL, first vertex, last edge and
       vertex) is mapped with `Final`, and `InternalHistory` (MakeWire's `Modified`, BRepFill_Filling's bindings)
       records each sub-shape replaced, or stays null. With the copy, every edge and vertex of the wire built so far
       was replaced, changed or not; now only the vertex that moved, the edges holding it and the wire are. The list
       form calls its first `Add` within its own change.
1414. **What the results share**, measured on frozen inputs (`ConstructionInputsUnchangedTests`): the overlay compares
       a working copy with its original as `KeepUnchanged` compared a copy (`IsSameData`), so the sweeps, lofts, fills,
       evolved shapes and twins share exactly what they shared. A prism of a polygon face holds the face, its edges and
       vertices; of a circle face, the vertex (the circle takes the cylinder's pcurve, decision 1102, unchanged); a
       revolution, the face's vertices (its edges take the new faces' pcurves); a face of a planar wire, the wire's
       edges and vertices. Lofts, ruled faces, pipes and BRepLib's tolerance twins write into every edge or vertex
       (pcurves, tolerances), as OCCT: their results hold new TShapes for them. The one change is MakeWire's (1413):
       it keeps the caller's unchanged edges where it copied them.
1415. **Seven oracle replays move to plan 3.2's second level** (`Tape.AcceptOtherArguments`, a new mode of the
       recorded tape: the calls must be those recorded, their arguments may differ): BRepFill's `Shell`, `ComputeACR`
       and `InsertACR`, MakeOffset's three random and build123d cases, MakeFillet2d's random profiles. Their inputs are
       wires the test builds with MakeWire, merging vertices; the wire now holds the caller's unchanged edges, which,
       frozen, keep the Free flag the copies had cleared, so the BRep text given to native differs in that flag only.
       Native's recorded results answer the same geometry; each test's own comparisons (geometry and topology, the
       Free flag masked) are unchanged and pass. The reason is `Tape.WireKeepsCallersEdges`. No other test moved; every
       suite keeps its counts.
1416. **The tests**: `ConstructionInputsUnchangedTests` in the kernel (17: prisms of polygon and circle faces,
       revolutions by π and 2π, pipes, smoothed and ruled lofts, a loft between points, the generator, ruled faces and
       shells, evolved shapes and volumes, projections on a solid and on a compound of its faces, half spaces, faces of
       frozen wires, wires with a merge, changes of published polygons and faces, BRepLib's twins): the inputs untouched
       (`ShapeSnapshot`) and the result holding what 1414 says. In the modelling layer (4): extrusions, revolutions,
       sweeps and lofts of faces taken from other parts leave the parts' BRep text unchanged, and an extruded face is
       shared with the solid with its edges (build123d revolves with copy, so a revolution shares nothing).
1417. **Measured** (`benchmarks/Kerf.Kernel.Benchmarks -- construction`, new: each operation on frozen inputs, Release,
       one thread, the median of 9 rounds; before is `main`, after this unit; other units ran beside, so times carry
       the machine's noise, allocations don't):
       | operation | µs before | µs after | KB before | KB after |
       |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
       | prism of a square face | 47.0 | 30.9 | 79.4 | 54.8 |
       | prism of a circle face | 16.2 | 15.5 | 36.3 | 31.6 |
       | prism and the history of every edge | 31.2 | 20.6 | 81.1 | 57.5 |
       | revolution of a face | 71.6 | 59.5 | 139.2 | 122.8 |
       | pipe of a circle face | 646 | 565 | 617 | 607 |
       | loft of three circles | 1,395 | 1,100 | 1,290 | 1,263 |
       | ruled face of two edges | 61.9 | 46.0 | 173.7 | 165.7 |
       | ruled shell of two wires | 123 | 82 | 343 | 327 |
       | evolved | 325 | 191 | 436 | 392 |
       | projection on a cylinder | 2,674 | 2,528 | 2,709 | 2,709 |
       | face of a frozen polygon wire | 41.9 | 30.8 | 136.0 | 127.5 |
       | face of a frozen circle | 41.5 | 34.6 | 88.0 | 86.9 |
       | wire of four frozen edges, merged | 4.7 | 4.6 | 6.3 | 6.9 |
       | pipe along a polyline | 589 | 475 | 900 | 872 |
       | BRepLib's TolerancesUpdated twin | 42.6 | 31.2 | 101.8 | 66.7 |

       Allocation falls by 2 to 34% wherever an input was copied whole (the twin −34%, a polygon face's prism −31%),
       and is the same where the copy was a small part of the work (the projection's section). The wire maker costs
       0.6 KB more per wire: an overlay for each merging `Add`, where the copy was made only when a vertex had to move.
       A first version made the overlay's working copies on writes that change nothing (a merged vertex's tolerance
       "raised" to its own value): 15.7 µs and 30.5 KB for the wire; the vertex's tolerance and point and the TShapes'
       Modified flag are now not written when they already hold the value (`WorkingOverlay.TakesWrite`), and a change
       that wrote nothing skips its assembly. 10H1's `WorkingOverlayTests` counted the working copy such a write made: it
       now expects none (the result, the input itself, is unchanged). Bento's benchmark (`Kerf.Kernel.Bento.Benchmarks -- 7 0`, 11 examples):
       serial medians 1,320 ms before and 1,338 ms after, allocation per example unchanged (802 MB for the largest,
       97.4 MB for the bottle). A run with other units' suites beside measured 2,441 ms; a run alone after it, 1,338 ms.
1418. **The survey recounted** (overlay-survey.md): copy at entry 66 sites (Booleans 0, construction 0, healing 35,
       offsets 5, fillets 2, features 7, other 17); frozen-shape checks 196 (construction 29, from 54; two new in `WorkingOverlay`); direct `_shapes`
       edits 43 (LibraryMakeFace's two gone). Section 6 gains the rule of 1411. Construction's checks left are
       geometry's (10G), BRepLib's writes skipped when they change nothing (needed outside an overlay), the sweep's
       `Closed` flag, BRepFill_Filling's bindings of MakeWire's history, the pipe shell's, and 1410's point section
       and `SameParameter`.

## Phase 10: unit 10H5, no copy at entry in offsets, fillets and features

1419. **The offsets run in working overlays** (overlay-survey.md section 6): BRepOffset_MakeOffset (`MakeOffsetShape`,
       `MakeThickSolid`, but the thickening mode: 1421), the pipes and spheres of BRepOffset_Offset, and BiTgte_Blend.
       Each runs OCCT's code on the caller's shape (in place inside an operation's overlay that takes writes,
       `BeginUnlessWriting`), and the result holds new TShapes only for what changed. The copies' re-keying goes: the
       closing faces, the faces with their own offsets, BiTgte's faces, edges and stopping faces are the caller's; the
       history (`Generated`, `Modified`, `IsDeleted`, the images) is direct, through `Final`. A caller's *unfrozen* input
       (a shell it built of frozen faces, as the offset oracle's) is worked on with its unfrozen TShapes copied
       (`WithUnfrozenCopied`, `UncopiedWhereUnchanged`, 10H4's twins' step): in place, the overlay's assembly replaced
       the caller's shell's children, and the oracle's next run on the same shell gave another result. The history maps
       such sub-shapes onto their copies (`InternalCopied`).
1420. **OC5805's offset surface is carried by the overlay.** OCCT enlarges the offset surface of the face it is given in
       place (BRepOffset_Tool's EnLargeFace, `SetBasisSurface`), and the lateral edges are then extended to it (decision
       1101). The port's `PutSurfaceInPlace` did it on the offset's working faces and skipped a locked (frozen) face; it
       now asks `WorkingOverlay.IsLocked`, so in the run's overlay the caller's face's working copy takes the enlarged
       surface and its pcurves move onto it (`ChangeCurves()` gives the working copy's representations), as on the copy
       before; the caller's face keeps its surface. Tested on OCC5805.brep's thick solid (bugs/modalg_2/bug5805_3: one
       shell of 7 faces, area 1,185.03, the input unchanged, surface for surface); the corpus cases keep their status.
       Outside an overlay nothing changes.
1421. **Left on their copies, with a reason: the simple offset's solid and MakeOffset's thickening mode.** Both build
       wall faces on the caller's free edges with BRepLib_MakeFace, which copies frozen edges at its own entry until
       construction runs in an overlay (unit 10H3). Inside an overlay the caller's edges are frozen, so a wall held copies
       of them beside the caller's own: face1.brep's simple offset solid didn't close (`ErrorInvalidNbShells`, where
       native gives a solid), and thickened open shells held their vertices twice (the offset oracle's replay diverged).
       On the copies the walls share the edges, as before. 10H6 converts both once 10H3's MakeFace runs in place in an
       overlay (`MakeSimpleOffset`'s copy and MakeOffset's `EnterCopy` are the two sites left).
1422. **A second MakeOffset run after `Initialize` clears the analysis.** OCCT's `Initialize` and `Clear` leave
       BRepOffset_Analyse's edge types and ancestors, which its next `Perform` appends to: on the same shapes a second run
       on one object fails (`UnknownError`). With a copy at each run's entry the shapes were new; on the caller's shapes
       the doubling showed (Draw-lite's `offsetload` and `offsetperform` twice). `Initialize` clears the analysis
       (occt-issues.md).
1423. **The fillets run in working overlays.**
       - ChFi3d_Builder (fillets, chamfers, FilletSurf's builder) works on the caller's shape: its maps, spines, data
         structure and common points hold the caller's sub-shapes (`ToWork` and `FromWork` go). A detached overlay
         (`EnterOverlay`) is entered by `Compute` and `Simulate` (FilletSurf's `Perform` and `Simulate`), which write the
         vertex tolerances and the spines' 3D curves; the first `Compute` with a result finishes it, and a later
         computation starts a new one, on the caller's shape as given (on the copy, a second `Compute` ran on what the
         first had changed, and kept the copy's TShapes). The reconstruction's Booleans are destructive in it, as on the
         copy.
       - ChFi2d_Builder builds the face's missing 3D curves in an overlay whose result stands for the face (decision
         854, in place of `BRepLib.Curves3dBuilt`), and `UpdateNewVertex`'s check asks `IsReadOnly`.
       - BRep_Builder's `MakeFace` and `MakeEdge` refusal (OCCT's: no new TShape into a variable holding a locked shape)
         asks `WorkingOverlay.IsLocked`: inside an overlay a variable holding a frozen shape takes the new TShape, as one
         holding its copy did. Found by the fillet corpus (blend/complex/A2, blend/tolblend_simple C5, C9 and D2,
         bugs/modalg_2/bug487 threw `TopoDS_LockedShape`).
1424. **The features run in working overlays.**
       - LocOpe's working shapes (`WorkingShapes`) are a detached overlay, shared by an operation and those it runs (the
         gluer's wires on the shape, splitter and generator; a BRepFeat feature's LocOpe sweeps and gluing), made at the
         first `Enter` (borrowed with `ForTool` inside an operation's overlay that takes writes). Each public call that
         writes, or reads what was written, enters it: LocOpe_SplitShape's `Add`, `CanSplit`, `LeftOf` and
         `DescendantShapes`; LocOpe_WiresOnShape's `Add`, `Bind`, `BindAll` and its queries; the spliter's, gluer's,
         generator's and draft splitter's `Perform`; the sweeps' construction; BRepFeat's makers' `Init`, `Add` and
         `Perform…` (`Form.EnterWork`). `Working`, `Copied` and `Original` go (the shapes are the caller's), `IsCopied`
         is `IsWritten`, and `Finish` takes the shapes as they are (the holder compound, the features' one direct
         `_shapes` edit, goes). LocOpe_SplitShape's `LeftOf` after the splitting maps the wire's edges with `Final`.
       - BRepFeat_MakeLinearForm writes the contour in a detached overlay from `Init` to the end of `Perform`;
         BRepFeat_RibSlot's same-parameter pass on the glued result, and BRepOffsetAPI_DraftAngle's `CorrectWires`, run in
         one each. The Booleans inside are destructive, as OCCT's on unlocked shapes (the features' were already, on the
         copies; MakeLinearForm's basis, not copied, now is too).
1425. **The tests stay at level 1.** Every suite keeps its counts; no test moved to level 2, and the Draw-lite groups
       (offset and draft corpus and commands, fillets, 2D fillets, features) have the same statuses case by case. Two
       tests changed because they tested the copy, not a result: `ChFi3dBuilderTests.TheFrozenInputIsCopiedAndLeftUnchanged`
       is `…IsWrittenInAWorkingOverlayAndLeftUnchanged` (the data structure holds the caller's shapes), and LocOpe's
       `WorkingShapes_CopySharedSubShapesOnce…` is `WorkingShapes_WriteInAWorkingOverlay_AndShareTheUnchangedSubShapes`.
       New: `OffsetInputsUnchangedTests` (7: the offset shell, thick solids with both joins, OC5805's thick solid, a pipe
       on frozen edges, the rolling ball, the simple offset), `FilletInputsUnchangedTests` (6: fillets on a box and a
       fused part, a chamfer, two computations on one builder, the fillet surfaces, a 2D fillet) and
       `FeatureInputsUnchangedTests` (9: four bosses, a rib, a split and a gluing, LocOpe's split over several calls with
       no overlay left open, two drafts), each checking the inputs untouched (`ShapeSnapshot`), the result frozen and
       valid, and the faces left alone shared; and the modelling layer's `FeatureInputsUnchangedTests` (4: fillet and
       chamfer, offset and shell, thicken, draft on parts taken from elsewhere, BRep text for BRep text).
1426. **Measured** (Release, serial, one machine shared with other units: the times carry its noise; before is `main` at
       fc22dc9b, built beside, run back to back). The new `Kerf.Kernel.Benchmarks -- features` runs seven operations on
       16 frozen parts (boxes, cylinders, a boss fused on a box and a hole cut in one, four sizes each), the fastest of
       three runs each.
       - Allocation: offset with the arc join 96.6 to 97.1 MB before, 94.1 to 94.3 after (−3%); with the intersection
         join 104.9 to 106.1, 104.0 to 104.3; the thick solid 118.1 to 118.3, 116.6; filleting every edge 183.4 to 183.7,
         181.7; chamfering every edge 173.4 to 173.6, 171.7; the BRepFeat boss 49.8, 48.1 to 48.2; the draft 12.0 either
         way. Each now writes working copies of the TShapes it changes, where it copied the whole input; on parts this
         small the copy was a few per cent of the work.
       - Time: in two runs each, 312 and 231 ms before against 279 and 223 after for the arc offset, 67 and 102 against
         171 and 91 for the intersection, 142 and 124 against 187 and 127 for the thick solid, 114 and 106 against 156
         and 88 for the fillets, 125 and 83 against 104 and 87 for the chamfers: within the machine's noise.
       - Bento's benchmark (11 examples, 7 passes, two runs each): the same results; allocation per example the same or
         lower, most where fillets and shells run (the bottle 116.7 and 115.9 MB to 96.5 and 97.3, nesting locations 43.1
         and 47.2 to 33.5 and 33.1, chamfer and fillet 18.1 and 15.7 to 14.7 and 14.5); median recalculation 1,885 and
         2,428 ms before, 1,304 and 2,611 after (the machine was loaded).
       - Tests: ModelingAlgorithms 4,785 (4,763 and the 22 new; 9 skipped), Oracle 383, the modelling layer 1,880 (4
         new), Draw-lite's offset, draft, fillet, 2D fillet and feature classes 15 (every case's status as before).
1427. **The survey recounted** (overlay-survey.md): copy at entry 71 → 59 sites (offsets 5 → 2, fillets 2 → 0,
