## Phase 10: unit 10K1, OCCT's bugs: Booleans, boxes, distances, hangs and spurious failures

1428. **BOPAlgo_BOP's fuse of solids checks every shared face** (occt-issues.md, unit 6F's first row). `BuildSolid`
       scanned the face-to-solids map with `i < aNb`, so a solid whose only face shared with another was the map's last
       was taken as untouched and kept apart. The scan now includes the last face. The case needs a solid adding no
       face of its own after the shared one: a ball in a hollow ball sharing its sphere, as a compound or a compsolid,
       fused with a box (`BOPAlgo_BuildSolidTests`: OCCT kept the two apart; now one ball and the box, with the ball's
       volume and seven faces). No recording or corpus case moved.
1429. **Parabola and hyperbola arc boxes contain the arc** (rows 259, 263, 264). BndLib's 3D and 2D parabola,
       BndLib's 2D hyperbola and GeomBndLib's parabolas added only the arc's ends and vertex. Each now adds the arc's
       coordinate extrema: for a parabola x_k(U) = O_k + U²/(4F)·X_k + U·Y_k, extreme at U = −2F·Y_k/X_k (inside the
       arc); the 2D hyperbola uses GeomBndLib's per-coordinate code, as the 3D one did. Tested against points sampled on
       the arcs and the analytic extrema (`BndLibTurnedConicTests`; the two pinned GeomBndLib tests rewritten). The box
       oracle's parabolic edges (`BndLibOracleTests`, three tests) move to plan 3.2's third level: the port's box, and
       its oriented box, contain native's.
1430. **Extrema_ExtCS reports the point on the line** (row 265). Where a line's range, clipped to the surface's box,
       is shorter than Precision::Confusion, OCCT passed a default Extrema_POnCurv's point (the origin) as the point on
       the curve; it is now the range's middle, the point projected. Test: a short line against a torus
       (`Extrema_ExtCSTests`). Two oracle replays move to the third level, accepting native's origin: BRepExtrema's twin
       scenes (a box edge at the origin, so native's origin was within 5e-8 of the right point) and Draw-lite's
       `distmini` on MODERN_Refrigerator_1.brep, whose contact points native reported at the origin where they are at
       (5e-8, 70, 150) and the like.
1431. **ShapeAnalysis_Edge::CheckOverlapping returns on a zero-length edge** (row 512). The sampling step is half the
       shorter edge's length; for a zero-length edge it was 0 and the loop never ended. A step that no longer advances
       ends the sampling, so the edge's one point is checked once. Test with a time limit (`HangGuard`, new in the
       ModelingAlgorithms tests): a zero-length edge on another overlaps it, one off it doesn't.
1432. **ShapeConstruct::ConvertSurfaceToBSpline gives up after C0** (row 702). When GeomConvert_ApproxSurface threw at
       C0, OCCT retried C0 without end; it now returns the last result (null if none). Test: a surface whose evaluation
       always fails returns null within the time limit.
1433. **A fillet's radius by a law follows the law** (rows 1552, 1763). ChFiDS_FilSpine's `SetRadius(Law, IinC)`
       built a composite law, dropped it and cleared the radii, so `BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet.Add(law, edge)` and
       `SetRadius(law, IC, IinC)` threw at Build. The law's range is now mapped onto the spine's, first vertex to last,
       and sampled at 33 evenly spaced points into the spine's (parameter, radius) pairs, which the fillet interpolates
       as it does pairs given directly (`FilSpine.LawSamples`; IinC unused, as in OCCT). `TheEvolvingRadii` checks the
       fillets against the volume they remove, (1 − π/4)·∫r² along the edge: a linear law within 0.01, a sine law within
       0.5. OCCT's own linear `Add(R1, R2, E)` differs from that integral by 0.18, as before.
1434. **MakeFilling's continuities map to the plate's orders** (row 1240). BRepFill_Filling passed the GeomAbs_Shape
       value as the plate's order: C1 (2) gave a G2 constraint and G2 (3) threw "The continuity is not G0 G1 or G2".
       Now C0 is order 0, G1 and C1 are 1, G2 and above are 2, for edge constraints and for point constraints on faces
       (`Add(u, v, face, order)`, the same mistake). Test: a half cylinder's filling for G1, C1, G2 and C2, its G0 and
       G1 errors small, C1 the same face as G1, C2 as G2, G2 a different face. The MakeFilling oracle's cases with a C1,
       G2 or C2 constraint move to the third level (their differences counted as intended). build123d.NET's
       `MakeSurfacePatch` already mapped its C2 level to G2, which now builds; nothing there to remove. Its test patch
       at C2 is valid and bounded by the same edges, but bulges (area 282 against 153 at C1): an order-2 plate against
       ruled supports, worth a look when the modelling layer's patch is reviewed (10M).
1435. **A pipe of a vertex gives the edges it swept** (row 1307). BRepFill_Pipe kept no edge table for a vertex
       profile, so `BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe.Generated(spine edge, profile vertex)` dereferenced null (an access violation
       natively). The sweep's own table of the vertex's edges is kept. Test: a vertex at a polyline spine's start sweeps
       the spine, each generated edge joining its spine edge's ends. The pipe recordings' vertex-profile cases (native
       threw at GEN2) move to the third level: everything before agrees and the port's GEN2 line names an edge of the
       result for each pair.
1436. **GeomFill_Pipe between two sections no longer fails on 3D paths** (row 1156). `Init(Path, FirstSect, LastSect)`
       read CorrectedFrenet's `SetCurve` result as a failure, but it says whether the plain Frenet frame needs no
       correction; the pipe gave up with ImpossibleContact on most 3D paths. The result is ignored, as the other `Init`s
       do. Test: on a 3D B-spline path the surface's iso at the end is the iso at the start scaled by 2 about the path's
       end (the sections' radii are 1 and 2). The sweep recordings' pipe-2sect (27 of 30; native ImpossibleContact)
       move to the third level. The corpus case bugs/modalg_7/bug31361, whose script requires tuyau's "cannot make a
       surface", gets Draw-lite's first override of an OCCT reference (plan 3.3; `DrawCorpus.IntendedDifferences`): the
       pipe is built. Its sections lie in the path's plane, not across it, so the surface's approximation error is 301;
       GeomFill_Pipe reports its error and leaves the judgement to the caller, as its other constructions do.
1437. **ShapeCustom_SweptToElementary handles the modifier's null face and faces not swept** (rows 1389, 1390).
       `NewCurve2d` read the surface of the null face BRepTools_Modifier passes when it asks whether to copy an edge's
       vertices, and the swept surface of a face that has none; both now skip the pcurve's shift, which applies only to
       a swept face becoming a torus or a sphere. It failed on most shapes with a degenerated edge (29 of the dataset's
       small brep files). Test: OCCT's bug26359_parabola.brep, a revolved parabola, converts to a valid face of the same
       area. ShapeProcess's recordings on DSE3.rle, DSEwithTol1.rle and cts20960b.rle (the operator failed natively)
       move to the third level.
1438. **The medial axis of one closed edge fails cleanly** (row 1121, guarded). MAT2d_Mat2d took the roots from the
       empty list of the one bisector never built (a null dereference). The map now reports not done. A real medial axis
       of a single closed curve is left (touch): the 2D offset never meets it, as it cuts a one-edge contour first, so
       only BRepMAT2d_BisectingLocus's direct callers see it. The test that pinned the exception asserts IsDone false;
       the four recorded full-circle cases (native crashed) move to the third level.
1439. **A loft of periodic sections with different knots unifies them** (rows 1181, 1182). GeomFill_Profiler inserted
       each curve's knots into the others; on periodic curves BSplCLib::PrepareInsertKnots mispredicts the pole count
       (row 82, touch), so the port threw Standard_RangeError, or the curves kept different numbers of poles. When the
       periodic unification throws, or leaves different numbers of knots or poles, the profile is now made of the
       sections' non-periodic forms (closed, not periodic), which unify. The test that pinned the exception checks the
       common degree, knots and poles and each curve against its section. Two AppSurf recordings (APPSM 12, APPSP 67:
       native stopped at its unequal profile) move to the third level.
1440. **CorrectedFrenet's sampling is bounded** (row 1087). InitInterval's next step, max(|S|/2, LengthMin)/|S'|
       with S = C' ^ C'', fell very low on offset curves, so a sweep's trihedron took seconds to minutes. After 2,000
       samples on an interval (`SampleBudget`) the step is at least the interval's length over 2,000; a turn of more
       than 60° still halves it. A bound on the step alone (1e-3 of the default step) moved regular B-spline spines'
       frames by up to 1.5% against native; 1e-4 left the offsets as slow. With the budget, the CorrectedFrenet oracle
       and the sweep recordings stay bit-identical. On twelve random offsets of B-splines
       (`Offsets_of_BSplines_set_quickly`) the six turned ones took 1.3 to 4.7 s and kept 16,709 to 32,205 samples; now
       0.1 to 0.4 s and 6,910 to 9,782 (the test asserts fewer than 12,000, and orthonormal frames).
1441. **Three rows reclassified to touch** (rows 1122, 1296, 1565). Each needs an algorithm's deeper rework, beyond
       this batch, and none hangs, so no guard applies. MAT2d_Tool2d::BisecFusion would need a curve/point bisector
       (Bisector_BisecPC) extended backwards, which trimming can't do; BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffset's failure comes from
       Bisector_BisecAna leaving its curve unset on some arc profiles (unit 5M's rows); Draft_Modification's 24 of 870
       recorded failures are several null dereferences, each needing its case understood. The 2D offset reports "not
       done" for the first two; the draft still throws a NullReferenceException. They stay listed, with this reason, for
       the modules' rewrites.
1442. **The tests.** ModelingData 3,145 → 3,149, ModelingAlgorithms 4,802 → 4,814 (9 skipped), the oracle 383,
       DataExchange 276 (1 skipped), the modelling layer 1,884: all pass; the new tests are the fixes' (one or two per
       row), and the tests rewritten to the corrected behaviour are the ones the decisions above name (the GeomBndLib
       parabola pair, `TheEvolvingRadii`, the profiler's, GeomFill_Pipe's, the medial axis's full circle). The moved
       recordings compare at plan 3.2's third level, each with its reason, but the CorrectedFrenet oracle and the sweep
       recordings, which stay bit-identical. Draw-lite's groups for Booleans (every fourth case), healing, offsets and
       drafts, fillets, filling, pipes and sweeps, construction and the medial axis were run before and after: one case
       changed by a fix (bug31361, overridden: 1436) and one by the machine's load (bugs/modalg_7/bug83's "too slow"
       check failed before, passed after); every other case's status is unchanged.
## Phase 10: unit 10H6, the end of copy at entry

1443. **The last sites run in working overlays** (overlay-survey.md section 6), all 20:
       - **MakeOffset's thickening mode and the simple offset's solid** (decision 1421's two): the run opens its overlay
         as the other modes do (`WithUnfrozenCopied` for a caller's unfrozen shell, `UncopiedWhereUnchanged` at the
         end). The walls, made by BRepLib_MakeFace on the caller's free edges, now write into the same overlay (10H3's
         MakeFace joins it), so they share those edges: face1.brep's simple offset solid closes, and thickened open
         shells hold their vertices once. The simple offset's `Generated` maps the modifier's images with `Final`, and
         its healing context is brought up to date by `Finish`, as `CopyAtEntry`'s was. `_entry`, `EnterCopy`,
         `FinishCopy` and `InternalOriginal`'s copy branch go.
       - **HLR's outliner** (decision 1095's copy): `OutLiner.Fill` outlines the caller's shape in an overlay, and
         `HLRBRep_ShapeToHLR.Load` opens one around the outlining and its reads of what the outlining wrote (the
         vertices' representations on the split edges), finishing it into the outlined shape. The data structure holds
         the caller's own faces and edges, as OCCT's: `InternalWorkingShape`, `InternalWorkingImage` and
         HLRBRep_HLRToShape's `WorkingImage` go. HLRAppli_ReflectLines' `SameParameter` of the 3D edges, which share the
         caller's vertices and write into them (they shared the copy's before), runs in an overlay too; found by
         `ReflectLines_MatchNative`, whose five cases threw `Standard_ImmutableObject`.
       - **The STEP reader's regularity and ShapeProcess's modifiers** asked `BrepTools.HoldsFrozen` whether to write in
         place; they ask `WorkingOverlay.IsWritableInPlace` (no TShape of the graph frozen: ported code's own shape),
         the same walk under the overlay's name.
1444. **Meshing: an overlay of the mesher's own, which leads to 10L's `ShapeMesh`.** `BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh` on a shape
       holding a frozen TShape (or its functional twin, `Meshed`) opens `WorkingOverlay.Begin` on it (its unfrozen
       TShapes copied first), and the triangulations and polygons go to working copies of the faces and edges;
       `Shape()` is the assembled result, frozen, sharing everything meshing left alone (a shape already meshed finely
       enough comes back itself), and `History()` is the overlay's. The overlay is the mesher's own even inside another
       operation's (nested, not joined), as the copy was: meshing gives a result; joining would put the meshes on the
       calling operation's shapes. A wholly unfrozen shape is meshed in place, as OCCT. Chosen over making the mesh a
       separate result now: it is a few lines, and it is what `ShapeMesh` (decision 1349, question 59) needs — mesh in
       an overlay, read the meshes back while it is open, drop it unfinished — with no throwaway work; a separate
       result now would rewrite the mesher's reads and writes (the incremental check, the post-processor, the
       consumers) before 10L designs the type. Two tests read the meshes off the model's faces and edges, which are now
       the caller's: they read them off what stands for those in the result (`InResult`, through the history).
       BRep_Builder's `UpdateFaceUnfrozen`/`UpdateEdgeUnfrozen`, which the survey counted as frozen workarounds, are the
       mesher's attach of a mesh left unfrozen until publication (decision 488), not a workaround for frozen shapes: a
       frozen face takes them in an overlay like any update. They stay, renamed `UpdateFaceMesh`/`UpdateEdgeMesh`.
       Making every attach leave meshes unfrozen was tried and dropped: design 4.1 freezes geometry when it is attached,
       and `FreezingTests` pin it (a triangulation shared by two faces keeps its purpose because it is frozen).
       `ShapeMesh` retires them with the faces' triangles.
1445. **The machinery is gone**: `CopyAtEntry` (301 lines), `BrepTools.ExactCopyForWrite` (three forms), `HoldsFrozen`,
       `KeepUnchanged`, `KeepUnchangedIn`, `CopyFrozenForWrite` and their private helpers (`BRepTools.ExactCopy.cs`,
       `BRepTools.CopyFrozen.cs`; about 1,000 lines with `CopyAtEntry`). `CopyData`, `CopyFlags` and `IsSameData` stay,
       in `BRepTools.TShapeData.cs`: the overlay makes and compares its working copies with them (decision 1361).
       `ReShape.ReplaceTShapes(keys, results)` is `ReplaceResults(results)`: the overlay never re-keys. kerf.map and
       `OcctTypeNames` lose `BRepTools_CopyAtEntry`. Draw-lite's in-place commands (decision 495's `InPlace`, the
       unify-same-domain command and its rebound history) run in an overlay on the variable's shape instead of a forced
       copy. The tests that ran ported in-place code on an unfrozen copy (52 sites in 32 files) take it from
       `TestCopies.ExactCopyForWrite`, a test helper doing what the library's did. `LockedShapeException` and
       `FrozenShapeException` stay: BRep_Builder throws the first on a write into a locked or read-only shape (31 sites,
       OCCT's refusals among them), TopoDS_Builder the second on a shape that isn't free, as OCCT.
1446. **One way in, and the API reviewed.** `BeginUnlessInside` (10H3) and `BeginUnlessWriting` (10H4) had the same rule
       under two names (`Current is { IsFinished: false }` and `Writing is null`); `BeginUnlessWriting` stays, its nine
       `BeginUnlessInside` callers rewritten. The API, each member with its doc comment: `Begin` (an overlay of the
       operation's own: twins, a published result's change, the mesher), `BeginUnlessWriting` (or join the one that takes
       writes: in-place algorithms), `Detached`, `ForTool` and `Enter` (a tool whose work spans calls), `Finish`, `Final`,
       `History`, `Composed`, `Images`, `Initial`; `WithUnfrozenCopied`, `UncopiedWhereUnchanged`, `CopiedIn`; `Current`,
       `Writing`, `Parent`, `WorkingCount`, `IsFinished`, `AttachContext`. `Input()` goes: nothing used it.
1447. **One rule protects published shapes: `IsReadOnly`** (frozen, and no overlay here takes the write). `IsLocked`,
       BRep_Builder's 31 refusals (OCCT's `Locked()`), is now the flag or `IsReadOnly`; `TakesWrite` is its complement on
       a frozen TShape; the TShapes' setters apply the same rule through `TryWritable` and `CheckMutable`. The 152
       frozen-shape checks were reviewed: none left only guarded a copy (the three removed were the outliner's, the
       mesher's and the STEP reader's walks); the 149 left are the rule itself, writes skipped outside an overlay where
       they would change nothing or a cache bit (the vertex tolerance already high enough, `BRep_Tool::Range`'s Modified
       flag, the sweep's `Closed`, a frozen component's Free flag), copies of a caller's published wire or shell before a
       flag is set on it by algorithms that run outside overlays (the draft's, the pipe shell's), and geometry's (10G).
1448. **The flaky gate test** (`ShapeMeshTests.ABigMeshComesOutQuickly`, 100 ms to copy out 100,000 triangles, 1,200 ms
       twice in merge gates). The copy isn't slow (11 to 12 ms warm, alone); the test timed one cold call, the first
       `MeshExtraction.Extract` with its JIT, on a loaded machine, and the copy allocated 6.5 MB of large-object arrays
       for 2.4 MB of buffers: it computed each face's normals on a copy of its triangulation. Fixed both ways:
       `ToolTriangulatedShape.TryWriteSurfaceNormals` writes the surface normals straight into the buffer (OCCT's loop
       body shared with `ComputeNormals`; the normals are those the triangulation would store, as floats), so the copy
       allocates 2.7 MB; and the test takes the best of five runs and asserts the allocation (under twice the buffers),
       which load doesn't change.
1449. **The tests stay at level 1.** Every suite keeps its counts; no test moved to level 2. Tests that tested the
       machinery, not a result, were converted one for one: `BRepTools_CopyAtEntryTests` (7) is
       `WorkingOverlay_HealingPatternTests` (the same toy healing algorithm and assertions, in an overlay);
       `BRepTools_ExactCopyTests` (3) is `BRepTools_TShapeDataTests` (`CopyData` through the test copy, `IsSameData`
       through the overlay); the pilot's comparison with the copy path compares BRep text with the in-place fix on a test
       copy (`The_pilot_gives_what_the_in_place_fix_gives_on_a_copy`; the sharing it also compared is the inputs-unchanged
       tests'); `OutLiner_FrozenInputIsCopiedAndUnchanged` is `…IsOutlinedInAWorkingOverlayAndUnchanged`.
       Counts: Foundation 2,297, ModelingData 3,145, ModelingAlgorithms 4,802 (9 skipped), DataExchange 276 (1 skipped),
       Oracle 383, the modelling layer 1,884, Draw-lite's classes 687 (with `OCCTNET_CORPUS_FULL=1`: the whole corpus
       runs 17,872 cases, OK 10,465, BAD 500, IMPROVEMENT 12, SKIPPED 6,825, FAILED 70, against 8W's OK 10,462 and
       FAILED 73; the data-exchange milestone's bugs/caf/bug31075, which measures memory, failed under that run's load
       and passed alone, decision 1293).
1450. **Measured** (Release, serial, one machine shared with other units: the times carry its noise; before is `main` at
       c5759a4a, built beside, run back to back).
       - Bento's benchmark (`Kerf.Kernel.Bento.Benchmarks 7 0`, 11 examples, two runs each): the same volumes, faces and

         locations 33.6 and 34.5 to 30.7, the prismatic solid 4.3 and 3.6 to 3.8 and 3.5, the bottle 96.3 and 97.4 to

1451. **The survey closed** (overlay-survey.md): copy at entry 20 → 0 sites, the helpers gone; frozen-shape checks

## Phase 10: unit 10J2, heap and collections, the rest

1452. **The rewrite tool is kept** (`tools/collections-rewrite`, not in the solution): a Roslyn pass over the solution and
       the two benchmark projects, from the compiler's symbols, one mode per NCollection class (`datamap`, `dynarray`,
       `indexed`). It rewrites the types (qualified names in using aliases too), the members, the copies, and the
       contexts where a value is written through a reference (a `ref` local or argument, an assignment, a mutating call
       on a struct value), adds the usings it needs, and lists what it leaves by hand. 10J's pass (scratch) was its
       start. Each mode was one commit; the hand work was under 30 sites a type.
1453. **`NCollection_DataMap` is `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>`**, iteration order unchanged (both are .NET's hash table).
       A missing key must still fail with OCCT's `NoSuchObjectException`: the algorithms catch OCCT's failures
       (`FailureException`), and BRepMAT2d's native recordings and two unit tests name the exception; a first attempt
       with the indexer's `KeyNotFoundException` failed them. So reads are `DictionaryExtensions.GetValue` (OCCT's
       `Find`, `ChangeFind` and indexer read), and writes by reference `GetValueRef` (`ChangeFind` written through, the
       indexer assigned), `SetValueRef` (`Bound`) and `GetOrAddValueRef` (`TryBound`). `Bind` is the indexer's set (its
       returned bool, used at two places, became `TryAdd` with the replacement OCCT does), `TryBind` is `TryAdd`,
       `IsBound` is `ContainsKey`, `UnBind` is `Remove`, `Find(k, out v)` is `TryGetValue` (its out variables
       nullable, 132 places). 258 files.
1454. **`NCollection_DynamicArray` and `NCollection_Vector` are `List<T>`.** Reads index the list; writes into struct
       elements and `ref` results go through `CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan` (the wrapper's own mechanism); a used
       `Append` result becomes the value, then `Add`; OCCT's `SetValue`, which grows the array with default-constructed
       elements, is `ListExtensions.SetAt`. 9E's fix took the block size as the first capacity lazily, at the first
       element; `List<T>` can't defer it, so the default 256 and 0 are dropped (a list grows from 4) and the 27
       explicit sizes (BOPDS's 3s, the meshers' reservations, the voxel grid's estimate) became eager capacities. An
       index out of range throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` where the wrapper's span threw
       `IndexOutOfRangeException`; neither is OCCT's, and nothing catches either. 133 files.
1455. **The indexed maps are `IndexedSet<T>` and `IndexedMap<TKey, TValue>`** (`Kerf.Engine.Collections`, 0-based),
       10J's design: a list of keys and a dictionary of positions; `Add` returns the index, `IndexOf` −1 when absent,
       `RemoveAtSwap`, `Substitute`, `Swap`; the map adds `KeyAt`, `ValueAt` (by reference), `GetValue`/`GetValueRef`
       (failing with `NoSuchObjectException`), `TryGetValue`, `Keys` and enumeration in index order. OCCT's removal was
       checked against `NCollection_IndexedMap.hxx`: `RemoveFromIndex` swaps the last key into the place and removes
       the last, so `RemoveAtSwap` keeps OCCT's order after a removal (.NET's `OrderedDictionary` shifts). KERF0002
       knows the two types (and no longer OCCT's four maps, all gone).
1456. **The code keeps its own numbering.** Indices the algorithms store (the Booleans' data structure numbers its
       shapes from 1, and so do the STEP and IGES models, BRepTools' shape sets and the healing tools) move by one
       at the call: an index going in is `i - 1` (simplified for literals and `x + 1`), one coming out is
       `IndexOf(k) + 1` or `Add(k) + 1`; `FindIndex(k)` compared with 0 is `Contains`. The 267 loops from 1 to
       `Extent()` whose variable only indexes the map now run from 0. Results are identical by construction, and the
       suites say so; the remaining `- 1`s go as each package is reworked. 346 files, about 5,000 edits.
1457. **What is left** (collections-plan.md): `NCollection_List`, `Sequence`/`HSequence`, the four arrays,
       `math_Vector`'s scratch, the shared empty lists, the Bézier classes' knot arrays, the surfaces' `NCollection_Array2`
       constructors, and question 55's transient base, which the arrays and sequences still use. Each is a unit's worth
       (about 21,000 references in all); the brief's fallback applies, as in 10J: whole types, none half-converted.
1458. **Measured** (Release builds of each commit, two rounds alternating base, DataMap, DynamicArray and indexed maps,
       on a machine shared with other units' suites, so timings carry 30% noise and more):
       - **Allocation falls, results don't move.** The Booleans (`-- booleans simple`, 407 cases) allocate **6.91 MB a
         Boolean against 8.25** (−16%), all of it from the dynamic arrays: the lazily taken 256-element first block was
         larger than most of BOPDS's and the mesher's arrays ever get; the DataMap step gives 8.24, the indexed maps
         nothing measurable. Bento's parallel round allocates **11.08 GB against 11.57** (−4%), gen-0 collections
         2,420–2,447 against 2,556–2,560; per example, from 0.3 to 4.5 MB less (nesting locations 30.6 against 35.1,
         the bottle 95 against 98, extrude until 139.5 against 143). Every example gives the same volume, faces and
         triangles in all eight runs, and the parallel runs match the serial ones.
       - **Time, inside the noise:** the Booleans serial 3,037 and 4,655 ms (base, the second under load), 2,929 and
         2,612 (DataMap), 3,105 and 2,426 (DynamicArray), 2,578 and 2,544 (indexed maps); parallel 2,304 and 8,154,
         2,357 and 2,932, 2,994 and 1,824, 1,891 and 1,873. Bento's median recalculation 1,570 and 1,204 ms (base),
         1,376 and 1,848, 1,326 and 1,317, 1,343 and 1,198; parallel rounds 9.1 and 7.4 s (base), 6.8 and 7.8 s
         (indexed maps). The modelling layer's suite: 22 s before, 19 to 32 s after.
       - **Tests**, the same counts as `main` at f3cefbf3 before each commit and after the last: Foundation 2,297,
         ModelingData 3,145, ModelingAlgorithms 4,780 (9 skipped), DataExchange 276 (1 skipped), Oracle 383, Draw-lite
         687 (the base run had one time-out under load, bug24157_5; after the last commit all pass), the modelling
         layer 1,880. No comparison moved off level 1. Two catches on the way: the missing key's exception (decision 1453),
         and a string concatenation that took the `+ 1` as a digit (`"basis" + IndexOf(e) + 1`, an oracle test's
         printer; the tool now parenthesises in a string).

## Phase 10: unit 10K3, OCCT's bugs: curve and surface evaluation, conversion, gp and data exchange

16801. **Raising the degree of a periodic B-spline keeps the curve** (occt-issues.md, BSplCLib::IncreaseDegree on
       periodic curves). `BSplCLib::IncreaseDegree` makes a periodic curve non-periodic by prefixing the knots l to
       Upper − 1 less the period and appending Lower + 1 to f plus the period, with null poles before and after the
       curve's own. It counted the null poles before from the multiplicities of Lower to f, and those after from l to
       Upper: each from the other end. When the two sums differ (most periodic curves whose multiplicities aren't all
       1), the poles were shifted against the knots and the raised curve was another curve; now each end counts its
       own. `Geom_BSplineCurve::IncreaseDegree` and the 2D curve inherit it, and through them lofts' section
       unification and fillets' spines. Tests (`BSplineCurveDegreeElevationTests`): 200 random periodic curves, 3D
       rational or not and 2D, raised by 1 to 3, equal to the original at 41 parameters within 1e-9; and a quadratic
       with a double knot raised to cubic. One oracle replay moves to plan 3.2's third level: the 2D B-spline curve's
       edit chains (`Geom2dBSplineCurveOracleTests.Edits`), where one raise of 30 has unequal ends; the port's raised
       curve is checked against the curve before the raise, and native's recorded poles make the curve the chain's
       later edits work on (`Geom2dOracle.SameStructure`'s `thePolesFromNative`), so they ask native what they asked
       when recorded. No other recording moved.
16802. **gp's seven rows** (occt-issues.md, unit 1's gp table; one commit, as the brief allows). Each is tested against an
       independent reference (`GpFixedBugsTests`, eight tests, all failing before):
       - `Direction3D.Mirrored(Axis3D)` takes the axis direction's Z for its third component: the reflection
         2(d·a)a − d, the vector's mirror.
       - `Matrix2x2.Multiply` reads the other matrix before writing, so squaring in place (`M.Multiply(M)`) squares:
         the matrix, 2D transformation and 2D affinity powers of 2 or more, against products of the factor.
       - `Transform2D.Multiplied`, rotation by rotation, adds the other rotation's translation when the other has one
         (OCCT tested this one's), as gp_Trsf does: (T1 T2)(p) = T1(T2(p)).
       - `Transform2D.Powered`'s compound branch no longer folds the scale into the matrix's diagonal, and, like
         `Transform3D.Powered`'s, scales the square's translation by the scale before squaring it. The 3D branch had
         the same mistake, which the 2D row's tests found: a new row, fixed here too (OCCT's gp_Trsf::Power).
       - `Hyperbola2D.Asymptote1` and `Asymptote2` point along X ± (b/a)Y (the far points of the branches), and the
         second no longer throws for equal radii; `Directrix2` is at the centre less (a/e)X, where the second branch's
         points are e times as far from the second focus as from it.
       - `GeneralTransform3D.Powered` inverts an affinity raised to a power below −1.
       One oracle replay moves to plan 3.2's third level: `GpOracleTests.Trsf_composition`'s powers of scaled compound
       transformations from the cube on (`SamePowerOfScaled`: form and matrix against native's, the translation
       against the transformation applied |N| times). The 2D rows reach no recording.
16803. **A torus's mixed derivatives change sign with their order** (occt-issues.md, ElSLib::TorusDN). The odd/odd and
       even/even branches of `ElSLib.TorusDN` now reverse when (Nu + Nv) mod 4 is 0 and 2 respectively, as the closed
       form's do; OCCT reversed neither, so (1, 3), (3, 1) and (2, 4) had the wrong sign. `DN_matches_closed_form`
       loses its exception for those orders; the test that pinned OCCT's sign checks d⁴P/du dv³ = −d²P/du dv and
       d⁶P/du² dv⁴ = −d⁴P/du² dv². One oracle replay moves to plan 3.2's third level: `Geom_SurfacesOracleTests`'s
       torus DN of those orders compares native's with the port's reversed.
16804. **An offset curve's third derivative is the derivative of its second** (occt-issues.md, the offset curves'
       CalculateD3 and EvaluateDN; one commit, the rows sharing their site). With N = p′ × V (or p′ turned in 2D),
       R = |N|, D = N·N′, E = N·N″ + N′·N′ and F = N·N‴ + 3N′·N″, the offset's D3 adds
       offset·(N‴/R − 3D/R³ N″ − 3(E/R³ − 3D²/R⁵) N′ + (9DE/R⁵ − 15D³/R⁷ − F/R³) N), the derivative of D2's
       term, and CalculateD3's D2 now adds D2's N term (3D²/R⁵ − E/R³) as CalculateD2 does, in both branches (R⁷ above
       or below the resolution). `EvaluateDN(3)`, through GeomAdaptor_Curve's and Geom2dAdaptor_Curve's offsets,
       passes D1 and D2 in separate variables, so the basis's D2 no longer overwrites its D1. Offset curves' `D3` and
       `DN(u, 3)`, Adaptor2d_OffsetCurve's D3 and the adaptors' DN(3) agree with each other and with a finite
       difference of D2. The two port tests that pinned OCCT's values check exactly that (offset 0.5 of the ellipse
       (3, 1) at 0.7); the grid consistency tests no longer allow the adaptor's DN(3) to throw. The trihedron laws use
       the spine's D3, so on offset spines their frames' derivatives change too, and CorrectedFrenet's angle law, built
       from them: `Laws_on_an_offset_spine_have_the_derivatives_of_their_frames` (Frenet and CorrectedFrenet on an
       offset of a helix: D1's frame is D0's, its derivative a finite difference of D0's; it failed before). Eight oracle
       replays move to plan 3.2's third level:
       - the offset curves' evaluations (`GeomCurveOracleTests.Offset_curves`, `Offset_at_singular_points`;
         `GeomAdaptor_CurveOracleTests.Curves` through `AdaptorOracleInputs.SameCurveEval`): D3's V2 against the port's
         D2 (away from the basis's cusp), DN(3) against D3's V3, native's values read as recorded, and native's DN(3)
         allowed to throw where the port's doesn't;
       - the trihedron laws on offset spines (`TrihedronOracle`, for Frenet's and CorrectedFrenet's three random
         runs and OffsetSpines_Short): D0 compared, D1's and D2's frames against D0's; for CorrectedFrenet only D0's
         tangent, its frame checked orthonormal, its intervals increasing over the range (19 where OCCT's law, sampled
         with the wrong derivatives, has 723, on one trimmed offset), its average law finite;
       - MakePipeShell's corrected Frenet on an offset spine (`CorrectedFrenet_on_an_offset_free_form_spine_timing`):
         that spine has cusps where the tube isn't defined, and the two sweeps differ by up to 0.09 (area 210.5
         natively, 204.8 in the port, 2πrL 198.7): the same topology, both valid.
       The modelling layer's lofts and sweeps and ModelingAlgorithms' sweep recordings don't move.
16805. **A curve on a surface has the chain rule's third derivative** (occt-issues.md,
       Adaptor3d_CurveOnSurface::EvalD3). The general path's linear form weights D1U by u‴ (OCCT: u′) and gives
       D3UVV 3u′v′² (OCCT: 5u′v′², its second V32 line repeating the term). `Adaptor3d_CurveOnSurfaceTests` drops the
       OCCT formula from its reference: the six evaluations that compared D3 with it compare with the chain rule, and
       the test that pinned the difference (a line of slope (1, 2) on a cylinder of radius 2, off by about 0.9) checks
       D3 against the chain rule and a finite difference of D2.
16806. **An offset surface transforms its parameters once** (occt-issues.md, Geom_OffsetSurface::TransformParameters).
       They are the basis surface's, as `ParametricTransformation` already said; the second transformation by the
       equivalent surface is gone. The test that pinned the double scale checks, for offsets of a plane, a cylinder
       and a sphere, with and without the equivalent surface, that the transformed surface's point at the transformed
       parameters is the transformed point, and that the parameters are ParametricTransformation's.
16807. **A B-spline surface split in V, from the larger parameter, is reversed in V** (occt-issues.md,
       GeomConvert::SplitBSplineSurface). The V branch tests V's periodicity and calls `VReverse`, where OCCT tested U's
       and reversed U. The test that pinned the U reversal checks the split's corners and an inner point against the
       surface with V reversed. One oracle replay moves to plan 3.2's third level: `GeomConvertOracleTests`'s splits by
       parameters in V that either reverses (`SameBSplineSurface` reads native's poles and knots without comparing; the
       port's U range is the surface's and its V ends are the isos at the two parameters).
16808. **The knot splitting of a surface smooth enough in V keeps its U splits** (occt-issues.md,
       GeomConvert_BSplineSurfaceKnotSplitting). When V needs no inner split, its first and last knot indices go to the
       V split indices; OCCT wrote them over the U ones and left V's null, so `VSplitCount`, `VSplitValue` and
       `Splitting` threw. The test that pinned the NullReferenceException checks the U splits (those computed with V's
       range 0) and V's two ends.
16809. **Canonical recognition finds ellipses at any angle** (occt-issues.md,
       GeomConvert_CurveToAnaCurve::ComputeEllipse). `ConicDefinition` takes the rotation of the conic's axes with its
       sign, cos 2t = (a − c)/√((a − c)² + 4b²) and sin 2t = 2b/√(…), and the longer semi-axis for the main axis;
       OCCT took cos 2t and sin t positive, so its axes were within 45° of the fitting frame's X, and gave up where
       a = c (45°). The test that pinned the rejection at 60° checks the arc turned in 15° steps all round: recognised
       at every step with its radii, centre and major axis (OCCT: 0 to 30° and 180 to 210° only). One case of
       `ComputeCurve_ConversionTypes` had relied on the bug: a rational quadratic arc with an end pole moved, meant
       not to be an ellipse, is one (any rational quadratic is a conic), now recognised; the failing case is now an
       inner pole of a two-span arc. ShapeAnalysis's canonical recognition tests pass unchanged.
16810. **GeomConvert_SurfToAnaSurf::TryCylinerCone's half-range point is left** (occt-issues.md; reclassified from fix
       K7 to leave). The point is taken on an end iso only when it isn't a circle: on a cone that is the apex's iso, a
       point, the same at any parameter (inside the range or not, its poles being one point). An iso that is neither
       makes the surface no cone, and the cone built through it fails the conversion's gap test, as it would through
       the middle point. No case shows a user the difference, so no test can fail first; the marker stays.
16811. **A cone's implicit equation holds away from the origin** (occt-issues.md, Geom_ConicalSurface::Coefficients).
       C1 to C3 and D are gp_Cone's, −T3j(radius + T34) and −2·radius·T34, where OCCT added radius·T3j and
       2·radius·T34. The test that pinned the wrong terms checks that a cone's points, off the origin with a reference
       radius, satisfy its equation and gp_Cone's. `Geom_SurfacesOracleTests.Elementary_surfaces` moves to plan 3.2's
       third level for the cone's linear and constant terms, compared with gp_Cone's.
16812. **The grid evaluation of an indirect 2D parabola follows its frame** (occt-issues.md, Geom2dGridEval_Parabola).
       The five evaluators take the frame's Y direction, where OCCT turned X by +90° whatever the frame's sense. The
       test that pinned the mirroring checks the indirect parabola's grid against its own evaluation, its points
       equidistant from focus and directrix, on the side of the mirror axis the frame's Y says.
16813. **An extrusion adaptor trims the direction it is asked to** (occt-issues.md,
       GeomAdaptor_SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion::VTrim, UTrim). The adaptor keeps V bounds (unbounded until `VTrim` sets
       them; OCCT had none); `VTrim` sets them and `UTrim` trims the curve, each keeping the other's. The test that
       pinned the swap checks the bounds of each trim and of both, and their evaluation against the extrusion surface.
       No recording moved: OCCT's algorithms reach extrusions through GeomAdaptor_Surface, not these trims.
16814. **A rational bilinear patch's cached second derivatives are right** (occt-issues.md, BSplSLib::CacheD2). The
       rows above MinIndMax of the work array are zeroed again for the weights' smaller dimension, so a max degree
       below 2 no longer leaves pole values where the weights' second derivative is read. (The triage found no marker:
       it was a comment in CacheD2's weights branch.) `CacheD0ToD2_MatchD0ToD2` drops its exception for rational
       surfaces of degrees (1, 1): their cached second derivatives match BSplSLib::D2's. No recording moved:
       BSplSLib_Cache, which the evaluators use, never had the bug.
16815. **STL read from a stream is recognised as from a file** (occt-issues.md, RWStl::ReadStream and
       StlAPI_Reader::Read(stream)). The stream is ASCII if shorter than a binary file of one facet or if its first 134
       bytes are all at most `~`, as RWStl_Reader::Read decides for files; OCCT took it for ASCII only if it began
       "solid", so a binary header starting "solid " (common from other tools), and ASCII starting "SOLID" or with a
       blank, failed. Tests (`RWStlFixedBugsTests`): a binary stream with such a header reads as the binary reader
       reads it, through StlAPI too; ASCII in capitals reads. RWStlNativeTests' eight stream lines where native gave
       NULL or FAIL (leadingblank.stl, upper.stl, and the binary files given a "solid " header) move to plan 3.2's
       third level: the port's stream read equals native's file read of the same data.
16816. **Every domain of a multi-domain ASCII STL is read** (occt-issues.md, RWStl_Reader::Read, multi-domain ASCII).
       The line buffer reads ahead in 1 KB blocks; after a domain, the reader now puts the stream back where its lines
       end (`ReadLineBuffer.UnreadCount`, an addition) before skipping the blanks to the next domain. OCCT went on from
       the stream's position, past the buffered data or at its end, so files under a block lost the domains after the
       first (twosolids.stl), and blanks skipped there could join lines at a block's end. Tests: a two-domain file
       under 1 KB gives both domains, and three domains read with the blanks between them moved across the blocks' ends
       (80 placements). RWStlNativeTests' five blocks of such files (twosolids.stl, as recorded, doubled, with blanks and
       with CR LF; OMF6391_box.stl with blanks) move to plan 3.2's third level: native's domains are the port's first,
       the whole-file reads hold all the domains' triangles, the stream readers are native's. The reader's return
       value is OCCT's: false after an ASCII file's last short block, whether its domains were all read or not.
16829. **A point on a surface keeps its parameters through binary BRep** (occt-issues.md, BinTools_ShapeSet's point on
       a surface). OCCT's writers put the second parameter first and its readers took the first for the first, so the
       two were swapped on every round trip. The readers (`BinaryShapeSet`, the table format, and `ShapeReader`, the
       position format) now take the first value written for the second parameter; the writers are unchanged. So
       binary BRep files don't change, byte for byte (BinToolsFormatTests, which check the bytes against OCCT's
       sources, pass as they were, and the round trip test finds the second parameter written first), and every file
       written before, by OCCT or by the port, reads right: its first value is the second parameter, as OCCT has always
       written it. OCCT itself still reads the port's files swapped, as it reads its own.
       The test that pinned the swap (`Point_representations_round_trip`) checks both parameters in place for the
       table format's versions 2 to 4 and the position format.
16817. **STEP rendering methods are read as written** (occt-issues.md, RWStepVisual_RWSurfaceStyleRenderingWithProperties).
       Its reader, and RWSurfaceStyleRendering's, which had the same tests (a new row), take the method whose name the
       text is; OCCT's `strcmp(...)` tests were true for every other name, so .CONSTANT_SHADING. was read for
       anything else and .COLOUR_SHADING. for itself (545 records of the corpus).
16818. **A styled item is written with its target, whatever its type** (occt-issues.md, StepVisual_StyledItem::Item).
       `StyledItem.Target()` (an addition) returns the item read or set; the writers of StyledItem and its eight
       subclasses send it, where OCCT's sent `Item()`, null unless a representation item, so a styled representation
       was written `$` and its colour lost (68 records). `Share` still names the representation items only, as OCCT:
       a styled representation stays a root of the model's graph, so XSControl's root lists and transfers don't move.
16819. **IsComplex lists every complex case** (occt-issues.md, RWStepAP214_ReadWriteModule::IsComplex): 800 and 802 added,
       so ActuatedKinPairAndOrderKinPair and RepositionedTessellatedGeometricSet are written as complex records, not
       `?()` followed by their components (30 records). The test that pinned the two checks IsComplex against
       ComplexType for every case.
16820. **BOOLEAN_REPRESENTATION_ITEM's value is written .T. or .F.** (occt-issues.md, two rows): `SendBoolean`, where
       OCCT's C++ promoted the bool to an int and wrote 1 or 0, which its reader rejects.
       The four rows above are checked by the STEP corpus round trip (`StepRoundTripTests.CorpusRoundTrips`: 338 files,
       1.5 million records read and written back): the causes they had there (NotComplex, BoolAsInt, StyledItemTarget,
       RenderingMethod) are no longer explained, and none occurs; every record they covered is written back as read.
16821. **Two reflectance styles and TESSELLATED_ITEM are named and read** (occt-issues.md, RWStepAP214_ReadWriteModule,
       cases 825, 826 and 708). SURFACE_STYLE_REFLECTANCE_AMBIENT_DIFFUSE(_SPECULAR) get their names in StepType, the
       type map and the writer's cases (OCCT had their readers only); TESSELLATED_ITEM, named by StepType, joins the
       type map. `StepAP214ProtocolTests` no longer lists them among OCCT's disagreements: every case of the protocol
       now names its type and reads back its case. The corpus has none of these records.
16822. **XSControl_Reader reads STEP** (occt-issues.md, IFSelect_WorkSession::ReadFile with StepSelect_WorkLibrary).
       The session gives the library no model; `StepWorkLibrary` now makes one for its protocol when none is given
       (and hands it back only on success), where OCCT 8's read into the null model and failed (RetFail).
       STEPControl_Reader, which makes its model itself, is unchanged. The test that pinned the failure now reads
       screw.step through a generic reader on a STEP session: RetDone, as many entities as STEPControl_Reader.
16823. **A 2D trimmed curve can be written to STEP** (occt-issues.md, GeomToStep_MakeCurve, Geom2d): the trimmed-curve
       branch now comes before the bounded curves', so the curve is written as its basis, as OCCT's unreachable branch
       meant; OCCT sent it to MakeBoundedCurve, which refused it (StdFail_NotDone).
16824. **A rational 2D Bezier curve keeps its weights in STEP** (occt-issues.md, GeomToStep_MakeBoundedCurve, Geom2d):
       written as a rational B-spline, as the 3D case and 2D B-splines are. Tests (`GeomToStepTests`): a 2D trimmed
       line and arc written and read back; a rational quadratic Bezier read back equal at four parameters.
16825. **GeomToStep_MakeAxis2Placement2d(gp_Ax2) is left** (occt-issues.md; reclassified from fix K8 to leave). Nothing in
       OCCT calls it (the conics' writers use the gp_Ax22d form), and a 2D placement from a 3D frame has no one
       meaning (which plane, which direction) to fix it to; 10L's public API decides whether it stays.
16826. **Angles are written in the file's plane angle unit** (occt-issues.md, GeomToStep_MakeRectangularTrimmedSurface,
       MakeConicalSurface). A rectangular trimmed surface's angular bounds and a cone's semi-angle are divided by the
       plane angle factor, which StepToGeom multiplies them by; OCCT wrote the bounds in degrees and the semi-angle in
       radians whatever the unit, so with the default radians the bounds read back 57 times too large, and with
       degrees the semi-angle read back wrong. `GeomToStepTests` writes and reads back both with radians and with
       inches and degrees. Three native comparisons move to plan 3.2's third level: GeomStepNativeTests' cases (now
       compared case by case: the 2D trimmed curves, 4; the rational 2D Beziers, 2; the cones and rectangular trimmed
       surfaces, 7, are intended) and its data/occ shapes holding such geometry (19 sets in each unit, compared by
       hash); TopoStepNativeTests' conversions in inches and degrees that write a cone, with native's entity count (17).
16827. **STEP strings and names of any length are read** (occt-issues.md, step.lex, 16,383 bytes). The scanner's buffer
       grows as a token needs (within ParserReadLimits.MaxFileSize), where OCCT's flex scanner, unable to grow its
       buffer, failed on a token of 16,384 bytes or more. The test that pinned the failure reads strings and names of
       16,380 to 600,000 bytes whole. StepFileNativeTests' 101 long inputs where native failed move to plan 3.2's
       third level: the port parses them (or reports the syntax error of a string run to the end), also through a
       stream returning 997 bytes at a time, as from memory.
16828. **A tab ends a STEP string as a space does** (occt-issues.md, step.lex, the end of a string): a quote followed by
       blanks, the tab now among them, and `)` or `,` ends the string; OCCT's rule left the tab out, so `'a'`, a tab
       and a comma ran on to a later quote. Its class's double quote stays: it decides only malformed input. The
       scanner test that pinned the run-on reads `'a'` there; StepFileNativeTests' one such input (string/003) moves to
       the third level: it parses as with a space in place of the tab.
16830. **The tests and the corpus.** Foundation 2,297 → 2,305, ModelingData 3,149 → 3,152, ModelingAlgorithms 4,814 →
       4,815 (9 skipped), DataExchange 276 → 282 (1 skipped), the oracle 383, the modelling layer 1,884: all pass. The
       new tests are the fixes'; the rewritten ones are those the decisions above name. The moved comparisons are at
       plan 3.2's third level, each with its reason. Draw-lite's corpus tests for STL, STEP, STEP with documents, XDE,
       data exchange, construction (lofts), surfaces from curves and the cheap gaps (B-spline commands) pass with their
       recorded status counts, so no case's status changed; no Draw-lite override was needed. The "before" run was
       those tests' recorded expectations, not a fresh run of the base commit.
